import Solidity.Frontend.Import
import Solidity.Tools.Run
import Solidity.Semantics.RunFuel
import Solidity.Semantics.RevertMemory

/-!
# Replay upstream typed ABI semantic vectors

The JavaScript adapter retains Solidity's native fixture bytes and supplies
checked scalar arguments or typed ABI input bytes. This command imports each contract through `solc_import`, then
executes the vectors in order on the typed interpreter, retaining storage and
rolling back failed calls. It reports observations, not proofs. Unsupported
vectors, import gaps and exhausted loop fuel cannot count as passing tests.
-/

namespace Solidity.Tools.Upstream

open Lean Elab Command Meta Frontend

private def str (s : String) : Json := toJson s
private def result (status reason : String) (extra : List (String × Json) := []) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj ([("status", str status), ("reason", str reason)] ++ extra)

/-- Resource failures remain inconclusive even when an importer embeds the
exception text in a per-function row rather than throwing it. -/
def resourceLimited (reason : String) : Bool :=
  ["heartbeats", "maximum recursion", "out of memory"].any fun text =>
    (reason.toLower.splitOn text).length > 1

/-- Preserve all importer diagnostics; an earlier warning cannot hide a
later resource failure. This result never certifies a runtime observation. -/
def diagnosticFailure (messages : List String) : Json :=
  result (if messages.any resourceLimited then "blocked" else "broken")
    ("\n".intercalate messages)

private def argument (j : Json) : Except String RawExpr := do
  let value ← j.getStr?
  if value == "true" then return .bool true
  if value == "false" then return .bool false
  let some n := value.toInt? | throw s!"invalid scalar argument {value}"
  return if n < 0 then .unop .neg (.num n.natAbs) else .num n.toNat

private def word : Semantics.CallValue → Except String String
  | .uint n => pure (toString n.1)
  | .int n => pure (toString (n.1 % (2^256 : Int)))
  | .bool b => pure (if b then "1" else "0")

/-- Resolve source ABI entries by exact canonical signature and compiler identity.
No source-local helper, retained override or special entry is a fallback target.
The row-only path supports native (non-source) replay controls. -/
def resolveEntry (C : Contract) (rows : List ImportRow) (signature : String) : Except String String := do
  let source := C.funs.any fun (_, f) => f.sourceDecl.isSome
  let candidates := if source then C.funs.filterMap fun (name, f) => do
      let identity ← f.sourceDecl
      guard (identity.declaration.isSome && identity.externalEntry &&
        identity.signature == some signature)
      pure name
    else
      let canonical (s : String) := match s.splitOn "(" with
        | [name, args] => name ++ "(" ++
          ((args.replace "uint256" "uint").replace "int256" "int").replace "address payable" "address"
        | _ => s
      rows.filterMap fun r =>
        if canonical r.sourceSignature == canonical signature &&
            (Semantics.lookupBy r.name C.funs).isSome then some r.name else none
  match candidates with
  | [name] => pure name
  | [] => throw s!"no imported ABI entry for {signature}"
  | _ => throw s!"ambiguous imported ABI entry for {signature}"

/-- ABI bounds retained by the source reader, including enum membership.
The JavaScript adapter separately checks canonical word widths. -/
private def inRanges (row : ImportRow) (vector : Json) : Bool := Id.run do
  if row.paramRanges.isEmpty then return true
  let .ok args := vector.getObjValAs? (List String) "args" | return false
  if args.length != row.params.length then return false
  let values := row.params.zip args
  return row.paramRanges.all fun (name, lo, hi) =>
    (values.find? fun ((param, _), _) => param == name).any fun (_, value) =>
      value.toInt?.any fun n => lo ≤ n && n ≤ hi

/-- External entry reading: retain actual failure data, but keep the supplied
transaction environment. In particular this is not a self-call. Existing
indexed guards generate concrete bytes before execution; no outcome is used
to choose a panic code. Call arguments here are ABI-decoded locals or checked
scalar literals; arbitrary effectful top-level argument expressions are outside
this adapter. Ordinary calculus entry points remain unchanged. -/
def entryProgParts (C : Contract) (pre body post : List RawStmt) : Except String (Blk C []) := do
  let all := pre ++ body ++ post
  let k := RawStmt.maxIdxs all + 1
  let ss ← freshenBlocks (C.vars.map (·.1)) [] all
  unless ss.length == all.length do throw "entry statement boundaries changed during freshening"
  let action : ElabM (SProg C) := do
    let P ← elabStmtsP C (ss.take pre.length)
    let Q ← withReader (fun sc => { sc with retainFailureData := true })
      (elabStmtsP C ((ss.drop pre.length).take body.length))
    let R ← elabStmtsP C (ss.drop (pre.length + body.length))
    pure (P ++ Q ++ R)
  let P ← action.runFrom' { funs := C.funs } ([], k)
  SProg.chain [] [] P

/-- Observe only source execution; ABI preparation and serialization retain
ordinary decoder/encoder semantics, including their failure policy. -/
def entryProg (C : Contract) (ss : List RawStmt) : Except String (Blk C []) :=
  entryProgParts C [] ss []

/-- A failed generated guard emits exactly its own bytes, independent of the
fixture's expectation and without evaluating a source body. -/
theorem entryGuard_failed {C : Contract} {Γ : Ctx} (code fuel : Nat)
    (g : Val C Γ .bool) (σ : State C Γ) (h : g.evalT σ = .ok false) :
    (panicStmt code g).runF fuel σ =
      .error (THalt.ofData (Semantics.encodePanic code)) := by
  simp [panicStmt, Stmt.runF, TRun.ite, h, boolT, TRun.seq,
    TRun.revertData, RevPart.evalT]
  rfl

/-- A successful guard preserves the entire typed state, including the
transaction environment, heap, storage and ledger. -/
theorem entryGuard_success {C : Contract} {Γ : Ctx} (code fuel : Nat)
    (g : Val C Γ .bool) (σ : State C Γ) (h : g.evalT σ = .ok true) :
    (panicStmt code g).runF fuel σ = .ok ⟨σ, List.prefix_refl _⟩ := by
  simp only [panicStmt, Stmt.runF, TRun.ite, h, boolT, TRun.nil]
  rfl

/-- Evaluating a guard can itself fail; that earlier failure is forwarded,
not replaced by the guard's panic code. -/
theorem entryGuard_prior {C : Contract} {Γ : Ctx} (code fuel : Nat)
    (g : Val C Γ .bool) (σ : State C Γ) (e : THalt) (h : g.evalT σ = .error e) :
    (panicStmt code g).runF fuel σ = .error e := by
  simp [panicStmt, Stmt.runF, TRun.ite, h]
  rfl

namespace ABI
open Semantics
private def dataName := "__upstream_data"
private def outputName := "__upstream_output"
private def argName (i : Nat) := s!"__upstream_argument{i}"
private def retName (i : Nat) := s!"__upstream_return{i}"

def shape : Nat → Ty → List (String × Nat) → String → Except String String
  | 0, _, _, _ => throw "ABI schema depth budget exhausted"
  | fuel + 1, T, ws, key => do
    match T with
    | .prim p =>
      if (lookupBy (key ++ "#enum") ws).isSome then throw "nominal enum ABI range needs a declaration adapter"
      if let some fn := fnRow? ws key then
        let some (_, _, external) := fnParts? fn | throw "invalid function ABI metadata"
        if external then return "function" else throw "internal function has no ABI value"
      match AbiKind.ofValue p ws key with
      | .uint n => return if (lookupBy (key ++ "#address") ws).isSome then "address" else s!"uint{n}"
      | .int n => return s!"int{n}"
      | .bool => return "bool"
      | .bytesN n => return s!"bytes{n}"
      | _ => throw "invalid primitive ABI kind"
    | .ref (.array T) =>
      if lookupBy (key ++ "[]#bytes") ws == some 1 then
        return if (lookupBy (key ++ "#string") ws).isSome then "string" else "bytes"
      return (← shape fuel T ws (key ++ "[]")) ++ "[]"
    | .ref (.fixed T n) => return (← shape fuel T ws (key ++ "[]")) ++ s!"[{n}]"
    | .ref (.struct s) =>
      let parts ← (structDef s).mapM fun (f,T) => shape fuel T (structWidths s) f
      return "(" ++ String.intercalate "," parts ++ ")"
    | .ref (.mapping ..) => throw "mapping has no ABI encoding"

private def typeExpr : RawTy → Except String RawExpr
  | .named s => pure (.name s)
  | .array T => do
    let e ← typeExpr T
    pure (match e with
      | .name s => .name (s ++ "[]")
      | _ => .call "#abiArrayType" [e])
  | .fixed T n => return .index (← typeExpr T) (.num n)
  | .mapping .. => throw "mapping is not an ABI type"

def needsCanonical (d : FunDecl) : Bool :=
  d.params.any fun (x,T) => !(T matches .prim _) || (fnRow? d.widths x).isSome

def validate (d : FunDecl) (inputs outputs : List String) : Except String Unit := do
  let actualInputs ← d.params.mapM fun (x,T) => shape 128 T d.widths x
  let actualOutputs ← d.rets.mapM fun (x,T) => shape 128 T d.widths x
  unless actualInputs == inputs && actualOutputs == outputs do
    throw s!"ABI schema disagrees with admitted declarations: {actualInputs} -> {actualOutputs}"

/-- Build both the canonical input probe and the once-only source execution from
existing typed ABI operations. Source calls retain their ordinary admission. -/
def program (C : Contract) (d : FunDecl) (f : String) (ctor probe : Bool)
    (bytes : List Nat) : Except String (Blk C []) := do
  if bytes.any (· >= 256) then throw "invalid calldata byte"
  let reserved := [dataName, outputName] ++ (List.range d.params.length).map argName ++
    (List.range d.rets.length).map retName
  if C.vars.any (fun (x, _) => reserved.contains x) then throw "reserved ABI observer name collision"
  if C.funs.any (fun (x, _) => [bytesLitName, abiDecodeName, "abi.encode"].contains x) then
    throw "reserved ABI builtin name collision"
  let ts ← d.params.mapM fun (x,T) => typeExpr (abiRawTy T d.widths x)
  let (_, decode) := abiDecodeHeads C dataName ts
  let declarations ← d.params.zipIdx.mapM fun ((x,T),i) => do
    let raw := abiRawTy T d.widths x
    match T with
    | .prim _ => pure (RawStmt.decl raw (argName i) (some (decode i)))
    | .ref _ =>
      if lookupBy x d.paramLocs == some .storage then throw "storage parameter is not an ABI value"
      pure (RawStmt.declMemory raw (argName i) (some (decode i)))
  let args := (List.range d.params.length).map fun i => RawExpr.name (argName i)
  let call := RawExpr.call f args
  let captures ← if probe then pure [] else if ctor then pure (if C.ctor.isNone && C.inits.isEmpty && args.isEmpty then [] else [RawStmt.call (.name "constructor") args])
    else if d.rets.length == 1 then do
      let [(x,T)] := d.rets | throw "single return shape mismatch"
      let raw := abiRawTy T d.widths x
      pure [match T with
        | .prim _ => RawStmt.decl raw (retName 0) (some call)
        | .ref _ => if d.retStorage then RawStmt.declStorage raw (retName 0) (some call)
          else RawStmt.declMemory raw (retName 0) (some call)]
    else if d.rets.isEmpty then pure [RawStmt.call (.name f) args]
    else do
      let targets ← d.rets.zipIdx.mapM fun ((x,T),i) => match T with
        | .prim _ => pure (some (abiRawTy T d.widths x, retName i))
        | .ref _ => throw "multiple reference returns need a typed return adapter"
      pure [RawStmt.tupleDecl targets call]
  let returns := if probe then args else
    (List.range d.rets.length).map fun i => RawExpr.name (retName i)
  entryProgParts C ([.declMemory (.named "bytes") dataName (some (.bytesLit bytes))] ++ declarations)
    captures [.declMemory (.named "bytes") outputName (some (.call "abi.encode" returns))]

private def findBytes (x : Var) : (Γ : Ctx) → List Var → Option (Idx Γ (.mem bytesR))
  | [], _ => none
  | t :: Γ, n :: ns =>
    if n == x then match t with
      | .mem (.array (.prim .uint)) => some .here
      | _ => none
    else (findBytes x Γ ns).map Idx.there
  | _ :: _, [] => none

def readBytes {C : Contract} {Γ : Ctx} (σ : State C Γ)
    (i : Idx Γ (.mem bytesR)) : Except String (List Nat) := do
  let .ok bs := (RevPart.mem .raw i).evalT σ | throw "unset ABI output bytes"
  pure (bs.map UInt8.toNat)

theorem readBytes_exact {C : Contract} {Γ : Ctx} (σ : State C Γ)
    (i : Idx Γ (.mem bytesR)) (r : HRef σ.H bytesR)
    (h : TEnv.get i σ.env = some r) :
    readBytes σ i = .ok (((σ.heap.get r).1.map (fun v => UInt8.ofNat v.val.toNat)).map UInt8.toNat) := by
  simp only [readBytes, RevPart.evalT_mem σ .raw i r h]
  rfl

def output {C : Contract} {Γ : Ctx} (σ : State C Γ) (names : List Var) : Except String (List Nat) := do
  let some i := findBytes (.user outputName) Γ names | throw "missing typed ABI output local"
  readBytes σ i

def canonical (C : Contract) (d : FunDecl) (f : String) (bytes : List Nat)
    (σ : State C []) (force : Bool := false) : Except String Unit := do
  if !force && !needsCanonical d then return ()
  let ⟨_,Q⟩ ← program C d f false true bytes
  let .ok o := Q.runF 1000 σ | throw "calldata requires lazy/noncanonical ABI decoder replay"
  let encoded ← output o.st (Q.outNames [])
  -- External ABI entry permits trailing data. In this adapter raw calldata
  -- observations (msg.data/assembly/host operations) are refused separately;
  -- only the declared argument objects are available to the source body.
  unless encoded == bytes.take encoded.length do
    throw "noncanonical calldata requires lazy ABI decoder replay"

end ABI

/-- Replay complete supported vector sequences. Fuel exhaustion is inconclusive. -/
def replay (C : Contract) (rows : List ImportRow) (data : Json) : Json := Id.run do
  let bad := rows.filter fun r => r.status != .elaborated && r.status != .skipped
  if !bad.isEmpty then
    return result (if bad.any (resourceLimited ∘ ImportRow.reason) then "blocked" else "broken") "frontend import gaps" [("gaps", toJson (bad.map fun r =>
      Json.mkObj [("function", str r.sourceSignature), ("status", str r.status.toStr),
        ("reason", str r.reason)]))]
  if let .ok reason := data.getObjValAs? String "blocked" then
    return result "blocked" reason
  let .ok vectors := data.getObjValAs? (Array Json) "vectors"
    | return result "blocked" "missing execution vectors"
  if vectors.isEmpty then return result "blocked" "no execution vectors"
  let tx : TTx := { msgSender := PrimTy.ofIntD .uint 103164821458651970696730694074090566015747358738 }
  let mut state := State.deploy C tx
  let mut deployed := false
  let mut deploymentFailed := false
  let mut observed : Array Json := #[]
  for vector in vectors do
    let stopped (status reason : String) (extra : List (String × Json) := []) :=
      result status reason (("observed", toJson observed) :: extra)
    if deploymentFailed then return stopped "blocked" "calls after failed deployment need the upstream empty-code host"
    let .ok signature := vector.getObjValAs? String "signature"
      | return stopped "blocked" "missing signature"
    let raw := (vector.getObjVal? "calldata").isOk
    let argsResult := if raw then .ok [] else
      (vector.getObjValAs? (Array Json) "args").bind fun xs => xs.toList.mapM argument
    let .ok args := argsResult
      | return stopped "blocked" "unsupported scalar argument"
    let ctor := signature == "constructor"
    if !deployed && !ctor then
      let .ok ⟨_, Q⟩ := entryProg C (if C.ctor.isNone && C.inits.isEmpty then [] else [.call (.name "constructor") []])
        | return stopped "broken" "default deployment does not elaborate"
      match Prog.runF 1000 Q state with
      | .error .diverge | .error .exhausted =>
        return stopped "blocked" "deployment exhausted loop fuel/resources"
      | .error _ => return stopped "broken" "unexpected default deployment failure"
      | .ok o => state := o.st.glob
      deployed := true
    let resolved := resolveEntry C rows signature
    let function := resolved.toOption
    let declaration := if ctor then C.ctor else function.bind (Semantics.lookupBy · C.funs)
    if !ctor then state := state.transactionEntry
    if !raw then
      if let some declaration := declaration then
        for ((parameter, _), arg) in declaration.params.zip args do
          if (Semantics.lookupBy (parameter ++ "#address") declaration.widths).isSome then
            let some value := arg.litVal?
              | return stopped "blocked" "non-scalar address ABI argument"
            unless 0 ≤ value && value < 2^160 do
              return stopped "blocked" "noncanonical address ABI argument"
    let rawProgram : Except String (Blk C []) := do
      -- Source enum cardinality may be narrower than its erased ABI uint.
      -- Primitive ranges have byte widths; other nominal ranges need a decoder adapter.
      let row : Option ImportRow := if ctor then rows.find? (·.sourceName == "constructor") else
        function.bind fun name => rows.find? (·.name == name)
      if row.any (fun (r : ImportRow) => (r.paramRanges ++ r.elemRanges.map (fun (entry : String × Int × Int × Option Nat) => (entry.1, entry.2.1, entry.2.2.1))).any fun (_, lo, hi) =>
          !(List.range 32).any fun k =>
            let bits := 8 * (k + 1)
            (lo == 0 && hi == (2^bits : Int) - 1) ||
              (lo == -(2^(bits - 1) : Int) && hi == (2^(bits - 1) : Int) - 1)) then
        throw "nominal enum ABI range needs a declaration adapter"
      let bytes ← vector.getObjValAs? (List Nat) "calldata"
      let inputs ← vector.getObjValAs? (List String) "inputTypes"
      let outputs ← vector.getObjValAs? (List String) "outputTypes"
      let d ← if ctor then pure (C.ctor.getD { params := [], body := [] }) else do
        let some f := function | throw "missing unique source ABI declaration"
        let some d := Semantics.lookupBy f C.funs | throw "missing source ABI function"
        pure d
      ABI.validate d inputs outputs
      let canonicalOnly ← match vector.getObjVal? "canonicalOnly" with
        | .error _ => pure false
        | .ok j => fromJson? j
      ABI.canonical C d (function.getD "constructor") bytes state canonicalOnly
      ABI.program C d (function.getD "constructor") ctor false bytes
    if raw then
      if let .error reason := rawProgram then return stopped "blocked" reason
    let program := if raw then rawProgram else if ctor then entryProg C (if C.ctor.isNone && C.inits.isEmpty && args.isEmpty then [] else [.call (.name "constructor") args]) else do
      let name ← resolved
      entryProg C [← runStmt C name args]
    if let .error reason := program then
      return stopped "broken" s!"call does not elaborate: {signature}: {reason}"
    let .ok ⟨_, Q⟩ := program
      | return stopped "blocked" "missing call program"
    let before := state
    let rangeRow : Option ImportRow := if ctor then rows.find? (·.sourceName == "constructor") else
        function.bind fun name => rows.find? (·.name == name)
    let badRange := !raw && rangeRow.any (fun row => !inRanges row vector)
    let outcome := if badRange then .error .revert else if ctor && !((C.ctor.map (·.payable)).getD false) && state.tx.msgValue.1 != 0
      then .error .revert else Prog.runF 1000 Q state
    let actual : Except String (Bool × List String × List Nat × List Nat) := do
      match outcome with
      | .error .diverge => throw "execution exhausted loop fuel"
      | .error .exhausted =>
        throw "execution reached a model resource bound (including recursive unrolling); not an EVM failure"
      | .error .revert => pure (true, [], [], [])
      | .error (.revertWith bytes) =>
        pure (true, [], bytes.map UInt8.toNat, [])
      | .error .panic =>
        throw "generic model panic does not retain the ABI panic code"
      | .ok o =>
        if raw then return (false, [], [], ← ABI.output o.st (Q.outNames []))
        let vals := localVals (Q.outNames []) o.st.env
        let count := if ctor then 0 else
          ((function.bind fun f => Semantics.lookupBy f C.funs).map (·.rets.length)).getD 0
        let values ← (List.range count).mapM fun i => do
          let name := if count == 1 then retLocal else s!"{retLocal}{i}"
          let some value := Semantics.lookupBy (Var.ofName name) vals
            | throw s!"missing returned scalar {name}"
          word value
        pure (false, values, [], [])
    let .ok (failed, values, bytes, returned) := actual
      | return stopped "blocked" (match actual with
          | .error reason => reason
          | .ok _ => "unsupported execution outcome")
          [("inconclusiveVector", vector), ("blockedVector", vector)]
    observed := observed.push (Json.mkObj ([("signature", str signature),
      ("failed", toJson failed), ("values", toJson values), ("revertBytes", toJson bytes), ("returnBytes", toJson returned)] ++
      if raw then [("calldataBytes", (vector.getObjVal? "calldata").toOption.getD Json.null)] else []))
    let stopped (status reason : String) (extra : List (String × Json) := []) :=
      result status reason (("observed", toJson observed) :: extra)
    let .ok expectedFailure := vector.getObjValAs? Bool "failure"
      | return stopped "blocked" "missing expected outcome"
    let .ok expectedValues := if raw then .ok [] else vector.getObjValAs? (List String) "expected"
      | return stopped "blocked" "missing expected return values"
    let expectedData : Except String (List Nat) := match vector.getObjVal? "revertBytes" with
      | .error _ => .ok []
      | .ok encoded => fromJson? encoded
    let .ok expectedBytes := expectedData
      | return stopped "blocked" "invalid expected revert bytes"
    if expectedBytes.any (· >= 256) then return stopped "blocked" "invalid expected revert byte"
    let rawExpected : Except String (List Nat) := if raw then
      vector.getObjValAs? (List Nat) "expectedBytes" else .ok []
    let .ok expectedRaw := rawExpected | return stopped "blocked" "invalid expected ABI bytes"
    if expectedRaw.any (· >= 256) then return stopped "blocked" "invalid expected ABI byte"
    let mismatch := if raw then (if failed then bytes else returned) != expectedRaw
      else values != expectedValues || bytes != expectedBytes
    if failed != expectedFailure || mismatch then
      return stopped "broken" s!"runtime expectation mismatch: {signature}"
        [("expected", vector)]
    match outcome with
    | .ok o => state := o.st.glob
    | .error _ => state := before
    if ctor then
      deployed := true
      deploymentFailed := failed
  return result "working" "all supported runtime vectors match" [("observed", toJson observed)]

syntax (name := upstreamBatch) "#upstream_batch " str " to " str : command

@[command_elab upstreamBatch]
def elabUpstreamBatch : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let input := stx[1].isStrLit?.getD ""
  let output := stx[3].isStrLit?.getD ""
  let cases ← ofExcept ((Json.parse (← IO.FS.readFile input)).bind Json.getArr?)
  let mut results : Array Json := #[]
  for entry in cases do
    let baseline ← get
    let path ← ofExcept (entry.getObjValAs? String "path")
    let outcome ← (do
      try
      let fixture ← ofExcept (entry.getObjValAs? String "fixture")
      let contract ← ofExcept (entry.getObjValAs? String "contract")
      let name := Lean.Name.str `Upstream contract
      let bytes ← IO.FS.readBinFile fixture
      let command := s!"solc_import {toJson fixture |>.compress} hash {hex16 (fnv1a64 bytes)} as Upstream.«{contract}» testing entrypoints"
      let env ← getEnv
      let parsed ← ofExcept (Parser.runParserCategory env `command command)
      elabCommand parsed
      let diagnostics ← ((← get).messages.toList.filter fun message =>
        message.severity == .error || message.severity == .warning).mapM fun message =>
          message.data.toString
      unless diagnostics.isEmpty do return diagnosticFailure diagnostics
      liftTermElabM do
        let term ← `($(mkCIdent ``replay) $(mkCIdent name)
          $(mkCIdent (name ++ `report))
          ((Json.parse $(quote entry.compress)).toOption.getD Json.null))
        let expression ← Term.elabTermEnsuringType term (mkConst ``Json)
        Term.synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing
        let expression ← instantiateMVars expression
        unsafe evalExpr Json (mkConst ``Json) expression
      catch ex =>
        let reason ← ex.toMessageData.toString
        let limited := resourceLimited reason
        let status := if limited
          then "blocked" else "broken"
        pure (result status reason) : CommandElabM Json)
    set baseline
    let fields := outcome.getObj?.toOption.map (·.toList) |>.getD []
    let pipeline := (entry.getObjValAs? String "pipeline").toOption.getD "legacy"
    results := results.push (Json.mkObj (("path", str path) :: ("pipeline", str pipeline) :: fields))
    IO.FS.writeFile output (toJson results |>.pretty)

end Solidity.Tools.Upstream

import Solidity.Tools.Common
import Solidity.Syntax.Splice
import Solidity.Semantics.Run
import Solidity.Semantics.Deploy

/-!
# `#run`: call a contract's function in the typed run

```
#run CallsExample.addTwo(3)
#run Coin.mint(1, 5) with msg.sender := 7
#run Counter.dec() with count := 2
#run Counter.dec() from (State.init Counter)
```

The identifier names the contract and the function: its last component is
the function, the rest a `Contract` constant.  The arguments are `sol{ … }`
expressions, typed against the parameters (`-1` at an `int` parameter).
`from σ` gives the state the call starts in (a typed `State C []`: its
storage, heap, ledger, funds and transaction); without it the contract
starts fresh, every root at its default (`State.init`), with no funds.  `with` sets the transaction, a comma-separated list of
`msg.sender := n`, `msg.value := n`, `block.timestamp := n` and
`balance := n` (`address(this).balance`), over the start state's; and a
state variable of a value type, `count := 41`, over the start storage.

**A call is a program of one statement.**  Nothing at the value level
instantiates a function: the call is written as `sol{ … }` would read it
(`callStmt`) — `uint _r = f(a, b);` when `f` returns a value, `f(a, b);`
otherwise — and elaborated scoped by `elabProgS`, which inlines the body
(`Stmt.call`) as for any other call.  The value returned is then the local
`_r` of the final state; of several, `(uint _r0, uint _r1) = f(a, b);` and
the locals `_r0`, `_r1`, … (`runStmt`).  The program is run typed
(`Prog.run`, `Semantics/Run.lean`) from the start state; a `with` word out
of its type's range is an error.
`DiffTest.lean` builds its calls the same way, but a call of several returns
as the bare `f(a, b);`, whose returns the inlined body declares.

The output is `ok`, the value returned, and the storage one root per line
(`fmtStorage`, of the typed storage); or `revert`, or `panic`.  A loop runs
by iterating it (`TLoop.runImpl'`), so a call that never ends does not
return.

```
#deploy Mini(7) with msg.sender := 3
```

`#deploy C(args)` deploys `C` by `Contract.deployT` (`Semantics/Deploy.lean`,
what the constructor obligation is read at): it runs `constructor(args);`
(`ctorProgS`, the initializers and the constructor's body) from the
deployment's typed state (`State.deploy`), whose ledger and funds hold what
`msg.value := n` sends; `with` takes the transaction's fields only.  The
output is `ok`, the funds, and the storage; or how it halted.
-/

namespace Solidity.Tools

open Semantics (lookupBy)

/-- The raw type of a value type, as a declaration spells it. -/
def PrimTy.raw : PrimTy → RawTy
  | .uint => .named "uint"
  | .int => .named "int"
  | .bool => .named "bool"

/-- The local a returning call's value lands in. -/
def retLocal : String := "_r"

/-- The call of `f` as one statement: `uint _r = f(args);` if `f` returns a
value, `f(args);` if it does not. -/
def callStmt (C : Contract) (f : String) (args : List RawExpr) : Except String RawStmt := do
  let some d := lookupBy f C.funs | throw s!"the contract declares no function {f}"
  match d.ret with
  | none => pure (.call (.name f) args)
  | some (_, .prim p) => pure (.decl (PrimTy.raw p) retLocal (some (.call f args)))
  | some (_, T) => throw s!"{f} returns a {Ty.toStr T}, not a value type"

/-- The call `#run` reports: `callStmt`, but a function of several returns
lands them in `_r0`, `_r1`, …: `(uint _r0, uint _r1) = f(args);`.  (`callProg`
keeps the bare call, whose returns the body declares, for `#difftest`: a call
with targets is outside the compiled fragment.) -/
def runStmt (C : Contract) (f : String) (args : List RawExpr) : Except String RawStmt := do
  let some d := lookupBy f C.funs | throw s!"the contract declares no function {f}"
  if d.rets.length < 2 then callStmt C f args else
  let vs ← d.rets.zipIdx.mapM fun ((_, T), i) => match T with
    | .prim p => pure (some (PrimTy.raw p, s!"{retLocal}{i}"))
    | T => throw s!"{f} returns a {Ty.toStr T}, not a value type"
  pure (.tupleDecl vs (.call f args))

/-- The call of `f`, elaborated scoped (`elabProgS`): its body inlined. -/
def callProg [FreshNames] (C : Contract) (f : String) (args : List RawExpr) :
    Except String (Blk C []) := do
  elabProgS C [← callStmt C f args]

/-- The state a contract starts in: every root at its default, no funds, the
transaction `tx`. -/
def freshState (C : Contract) (tx : TTx := {}) (balance : PrimTy.uint.Denote := PrimTy.dflt .uint) :
    State C [] :=
  { State.init C with selfBalance := balance, tx }

/-- `StandardExample` fresh, with funds (`address(this).balance`) for the
examples' transfers to read. -/
def _root_.Solidity.State.exampleStore : State StandardExample [] :=
  freshState StandardExample (balance := PrimTy.ofIntD .uint 1000000000)

/-- `TestSuite` fresh, with funds like `State.exampleStore`. -/
def _root_.Solidity.State.testSuiteStore : State TestSuite [] :=
  freshState TestSuite (balance := PrimTy.ofIntD .uint 1000000000)

/-- An integer read at the type `p`, or the error `#run` reports. -/
def ofIntE (p : PrimTy) (n : Int) : Except String p.Denote :=
  match PrimTy.ofInt? p n with
  | some v => pure v
  | none => throw "the start state is not of the contract's types"

/-- `σ` with the transaction fields given replaced; an error where one is
not a `uint`. -/
def State.withTx {C : Contract} (σ : State C []) (sender value time balance : Option Int) :
    Except String (State C []) := do
  let w (n : Option Int) (d : PrimTy.uint.Denote) := match n with
    | some n => ofIntE .uint n
    | none => pure d
  pure { σ with
    tx := { σ.tx with msgSender := ← w sender σ.tx.msgSender, msgValue := ← w value σ.tx.msgValue,
                      timestamp := ← w time σ.tx.timestamp }
    selfBalance := ← w balance σ.selfBalance }

/-- `σ` with the state variable `r`, of a value type, set to `v`; an error
where `r` is no such variable or `v` not of its type. -/
def State.withRoot {C : Contract} (σ : State C []) (r : Name) (v : Semantics.CallValue) :
    Except String (State C []) :=
  match h : lookupBy r C.vars with
  | some (.prim p) => match v.as? p with
    | some y => pure { σ with storage := SFields.set (σ.storage : SFields C.vars) h (.prim y) }
    | none => throw "the start state is not of the contract's types"
  | some T => throw s!"{r} is a {Ty.toStr T}, not a value type"
  | none => throw s!"{r} is not a state variable"

/-- A state variable's integer given to `#run`, read at its type `p`. -/
def rootInt (r : Name) (p : PrimTy) (n : Int) : Except String (Name × Semantics.CallValue) :=
  return (r, .ofTyped (← ofIntE p n))

/-- `σ` with the state variables given replaced, in order. -/
def State.withRoots {C : Contract} (σ : State C []) (roots : List (Name × Semantics.CallValue)) :
    Except String (State C []) :=
  roots.foldlM (fun σ (r, v) => State.withRoot σ r v) σ

/-- **A scoped block run from a typed state**, in the typed run: `P` run
by `Prog.run` from `σ`, its end state or how it halted. -/
def _root_.Solidity.Prog.runT {C : Contract} {Γ' : Ctx} (σ : State C []) (P : Prog C [] Γ') :
    TRes (State C Γ') :=
  (Prog.run σ P).map (·.st)

/-- The locals of a typed environment, innermost first: each one's level at
base `0` (`Evm.lvl`), and its type and value if it is a value local. -/
def localCells {C : Contract} {H : HTy} : (Γ : Ctx) → TEnv C H Γ →
    List (Nat × Option ((p : PrimTy) × p.Denote))
  | [], _ => []
  | t :: Γ, e =>
    (match t, e.1 with
      | .val p, v => (Γ.length, some ⟨p, v⟩)
      | _, _ => (Γ.length, none)) :: localCells Γ e.2

/-- The value locals of a typed environment, by the names of its context. -/
def localVals {C : Contract} {H : HTy} {Γ : Ctx} (names : List Var)
    (e : TEnv C H Γ) : List (Var × Semantics.CallValue) :=
  (names.zip (localCells Γ e)).filterMap fun (x, _, c) => c.map fun v => (x, .ofTyped v.2)

/-- What the value local `x` holds after `P` runs from `σ` (`Prog.runT`):
`none` where the end state has no value local of that name. -/
def _root_.Solidity.Prog.localAfterT [FreshNames] {C : Contract} {Γ' : Ctx} (σ : State C [])
    (P : Prog C [] Γ') (x : String) : TRes (Option Semantics.CallValue) := do
  let τ ← Prog.runT σ P
  pure (lookupBy (Var.ofName x) (localVals (P.outNames []) τ.env))

/-- What `#run` prints: the outcome, the value returned, the storage. -/
def runReport [FreshNames] (C : Contract) (σ : State C []) (f : String) (args : List RawExpr) :
    Except String (List String) := do
  let ⟨_, Q⟩ ← elabProgS C [← runStmt C f args]
  let n : Nat := ((lookupBy f C.funs).map (·.rets.length)).getD 0
  pure <| match Prog.run σ Q with
    | .error h => [fmtHalt h]
    | .ok o =>
      let vals := localVals (Q.outNames []) o.st.env
      let ret := if n ≥ 2 then
          let vs := (List.range n).filterMap fun i => lookupBy (Var.ofName s!"{retLocal}{i}") vals
          [s!"returns ({", ".intercalate (vs.map CallValue.fmt)})"]
        else match lookupBy (Var.ofName retLocal) vals with
          | some v => [s!"returns {CallValue.fmt v}"]
          | none => []
      ["ok"] ++ ret ++ fmtStorage C o.st.storage

/-- One field of the transaction, `msg.sender := 7`, or a state variable,
`count := 41`. -/
syntax runEnv := ident " := " term:max

/-- `#run C.f(a, b) [from σ] [with msg.sender := n, count := m, …]`: run the
call in the typed run and print its outcome. -/
syntax (name := runCmd) "#run " ident "(" sol_expr,* ")" (" from " term:max)?
  (" with " runEnv,+)? : command

open Lean Elab Command Term Meta in
@[command_elab runCmd] def elabRun : CommandElab
  | `(#run $callee:ident ( $args:sol_expr,* ) $[from $σ?]? $[with $envs?,*]?) =>
    liftTermElabM do
    let (c, C, f) ← resolveFunction "#run" callee.getId
    let args ← liftMacroM <| args.getElems.mapM expandExpr
    let mut sender : Lean.Term ← `(none)
    let mut value : Lean.Term ← `(none)
    let mut time : Lean.Term ← `(none)
    let mut bal : Lean.Term ← `(none)
    let mut roots : Array Lean.Term := #[]
    for e in (envs?.map (·.getElems)).getD #[] do
      let `(runEnv| $k:ident := $v) := e | throwErrorAt e "#run: expected `name := value`"
      let n := (k.getId.toString false)
      match n with
      | "msg.sender" => sender ← `(some ($v : Int))
      | "msg.value" => value ← `(some ($v : Int))
      | "block.timestamp" => time ← `(some ($v : Int))
      | "balance" => bal ← `(some ($v : Int))
      | _ =>
        match Semantics.lookupBy n C.vars with
        | some (.prim .bool) =>
          roots := roots.push (← `(pure ($(quote n), Solidity.Semantics.CallValue.bool ($v : Bool))))
        | some (.prim .uint) => roots := roots.push (← `(Solidity.Tools.rootInt $(quote n) .uint ($v : Int)))
        | some (.prim .int) => roots := roots.push (← `(Solidity.Tools.rootInt $(quote n) .int ($v : Int)))
        | some T => throwErrorAt k "#run: {n} is a {Ty.toStr T}: give it with `from`"
        | none => throwErrorAt k "#run: {n} is not one of msg.sender, msg.value, \
            block.timestamp, balance, nor a state variable of {c}"
    let Ct := mkCIdent c
    let σ ← match σ? with
      | some σ => `(($σ : Solidity.State $Ct []))
      | none => `(freshState $Ct)
    let t ← `(do
      let σ ← State.withTx $σ $sender $value $time $bal
      let roots ← ([$roots,*] : List (Except String (Solidity.Name × Solidity.Semantics.CallValue))).mapM id
      let σ ← State.withRoots σ roots
      runReport $Ct σ $(quote f) [$args,*])
    logInfo (String.intercalate "\n" (← evalLines "#run" t))
  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

/-- What `#deploy` prints: the outcome of `Contract.deployT` (a
constructor that is not `payable` refuses value, else `constructor(args);`
runs from `State.deploy`), the contract's funds and its storage. -/
def deployReport [FreshNames] (C : Contract) (args : List RawExpr) (sender value time : Int) :
    Except String (List String) := do
  let ⟨_, Q⟩ ← ctorProgS C args
  let some tx := (do
      pure ({ msgSender := ← PrimTy.ofInt? .uint sender, msgValue := ← PrimTy.ofInt? .uint value,
              timestamp := ← PrimTy.ofInt? .uint time } : TTx))
    | throw "the deployment's start is not of the contract's types"
  pure <| match Contract.deployT C Q tx with
    | .error h => [fmtHalt h]
    | .ok σ => ["ok", s!"balance {σ.selfBalance.1}"] ++ fmtStorage C σ.storage

/-- `#deploy C(a, b) [with msg.sender := n, msg.value := m, …]`: deploy the
contract `C` in the typed run and print its outcome. -/
syntax (name := deployCmd) "#deploy " ident "(" sol_expr,* ")" (" with " runEnv,+)? : command

open Lean Elab Command Term Meta in
@[command_elab deployCmd] def elabDeploy : CommandElab
  | `(#deploy $c:ident ( $args:sol_expr,* ) $[with $envs?,*]?) => liftTermElabM do
    let some c ← contractConst? c.getId | throwErrorAt c "#deploy: {c.getId} is not a contract"
    let args ← liftMacroM <| args.getElems.mapM expandExpr
    let mut sender : Lean.Term ← `(0)
    let mut value : Lean.Term ← `(0)
    let mut time : Lean.Term ← `(0)
    for e in (envs?.map (·.getElems)).getD #[] do
      let `(runEnv| $k:ident := $v) := e | throwErrorAt e "#deploy: expected `name := value`"
      match (k.getId.toString false) with
      | "msg.sender" => sender := v
      | "msg.value" => value := v
      | "block.timestamp" => time := v
      | n => throwErrorAt k "#deploy: {n} is not one of msg.sender, msg.value, block.timestamp"
    let t ← `(deployReport $(mkCIdent c) [$args,*] ($sender : Int) ($value : Int) ($time : Int))
    logInfo (String.intercalate "\n" (← evalLines "#deploy" t))
  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

end Solidity.Tools

import Solidity.Semantics.Deploy

/-!
# A contract's lifetime, from successful deployment

The interface is explicit: a model supplies constructor calls and a family of
external entry calls, elaborated at the contract's types. Only those calls
generate transitions. Persistent states forget the transaction's heap and
locals; entering a call creates them afresh and books its incoming payment.

This is the deterministic run's reading, not a realization of callback havoc.
Successful execution is required for a commit. Revert and panic roll back the
payment and all writes, while time may advance. Divergence and exhaustion have
no completed-call transition. Waiting is explicit, including stuttering.

`AG`, `EF` and `AGEF` are a small temporal interface over finite execution
witnesses, not a claim of universal eventual progress or a full CTL language.
-/

namespace Solidity.Lifetime

variable {C : Contract}

/-- What survives between transactions. The address is fixed, time can advance. -/
structure World (C : Contract) where
  storage : Storage C
  net : Ledger
  balance : PrimTy.uint.Denote
  address : PrimTy.uint.Denote
  timestamp : PrimTy.uint.Denote

/-- Discard the completed call's memory and locals. -/
def World.ofState {Γ : Ctx} (σ : State C Γ) : World C :=
  ⟨Storage.resetTransient σ.storage, σ.net, σ.selfBalance, σ.tx.selfAddress, σ.tx.timestamp⟩

/-- Observe a persistent state without adding a payment or a caller's frame.
Predicates reading caller, value, oracle replies or memory are not persistent
predicates; use them in entry obligations instead. -/
def World.observe (s : World C) : State C [] :=
  { storage := Storage.resetTransient s.storage, H := [], heap := Heap.empty, env := (), net := s.net,
    selfBalance := s.balance, tx := { selfAddress := s.address, timestamp := s.timestamp } }

/-- Waiting and failed transactions can advance time without changing funds. -/
def World.atTime (s : World C) (t : PrimTy.uint.Denote) : World C :=
  { s with timestamp := t }

/-- A fresh transaction frame, with its incoming value credited once.
Insufficient sender funds are an environment restriction: this model has no
ledger of the environment's spendable balances. -/
def World.enter (s : World C) (tx : TTx) : TRes (State C []) := do
  let balance ← TRes.ofOpt (PrimTy.ofInt? .uint (s.balance.1 + tx.msgValue.1))
  pure {
    storage := Storage.resetTransient s.storage, H := [], heap := Heap.empty, env := (),
    net := if tx.msgValue.1 = 0 then s.net else
      Semantics.setBy tx.msgSender
        ((Semantics.lookupBy tx.msgSender s.net).getD 0 + tx.msgValue.1) s.net,
    selfBalance := balance, tx }

/-- Entering a transaction clears transient cells and preserves persistent roots. -/
theorem World.enter_storage {s : World C} {tx : TTx} {σ : State C []}
    (h : s.enter tx = .ok σ) : σ.storage = Storage.resetTransient s.storage := by
  unfold World.enter at h
  cases hb : PrimTy.ofInt? .uint (s.balance.1 + tx.msgValue.1) with
  | none => simp only [hb, TRes.ofOpt, bind, Except.bind] at h; cases h
  | some balance =>
    simp only [hb, TRes.ofOpt, bind, Except.bind] at h
    cases h
    rfl

/-- A zero-value call recreates only the transaction's ephemeral frame. -/
theorem World.enter_zero (s : World C) (tx : TTx) (zero : tx.msgValue.1 = 0) :
    s.enter tx = .ok { s.observe with tx := tx } := by
  simp only [World.enter, zero, Int.add_zero, PrimTy.ofInt?, s.balance.2,
    dite_true, TRes.ofOpt, bind, Except.bind, if_true]
  rfl

/-- An external transaction keeps the deployed address and cannot go back in
time. Self-calls belong inside the program, not to top-level transactions. -/
def World.accepts (s : World C) (tx : TTx) : Prop :=
  tx.selfAddress = s.address ∧ s.timestamp.1 ≤ tx.timestamp.1 ∧ tx.msgSender ≠ s.address

/-- The explicitly admitted interface. `deploy` is `constructor(args);`,
`call` is an externally callable `f(args);`, each with its frame closed.
Visibility is not retained by `Contract`: selecting this interface is a model
obligation. `D` and `A` can carry typed constructor and function inputs.
Environment predicates restrict funding, callers, oracle replies, and time. -/
structure System (C : Contract) (D A : Type) where
  deploy : D → Prog C [] []
  call : A → Prog C [] []
  payable : A → Bool := fun _ => false
  allowDeploy : D → TTx → Prop := fun _ _ => True
  allowCall : World C → A → TTx → Prop := fun _ _ _ => True

variable {D A : Type}

/-- Run exactly one entry call. The result is committed only when it is `ok`. -/
def System.run (M : System C D A) (s : World C) (a : A) (tx : TTx) : TRes (World C) := do
  if !M.payable a && tx.msgValue.1 != 0 then .error .revert else do
    let σ ← s.enter tx
    let o ← (M.call a).run σ
    pure (World.ofState o.st)

/-- A successful call has a fresh entry frame and an actual successful run;
exhaustion is never a witness to this theorem. -/
theorem System.run_ok {M : System C D A} {s t : World C} {a : A} {tx : TTx}
    (h : M.run s a tx = .ok t) :
    ∃ (σ : State C []) (o : Out C σ.H []),
      s.enter tx = .ok σ ∧ (M.call a).run σ = .ok o ∧ World.ofState o.st = t := by
  unfold System.run at h
  split at h
  · cases h
  · cases he : s.enter tx with
    | error e => simp only [he, bind, Except.bind] at h; cases h
    | ok σ =>
      simp only [he, bind, Except.bind] at h
      cases hr : (M.call a).run σ with
      | error e => simp only [hr] at h; cases h
      | ok o =>
        simp only [hr] at h
        exact ⟨σ, o, rfl, hr, Except.ok.inj h⟩

/-- Successful deployment alone initializes the lifetime; neither a default
storage nor an exhausted constructor is an initial deployed state. -/
def System.Init (M : System C D A) (s : World C) : Prop :=
  ∃ d tx σ, M.allowDeploy d tx ∧ C.deployT (M.deploy d) tx = .ok σ ∧ World.ofState σ = s

/-- Observable actions include inactivity, so progress cannot follow merely
from deleting executions where nobody calls the contract. -/
inductive Event (A : Type) where
  | call (action : A) (tx : TTx)
  | wait (timestamp : PrimTy.uint.Denote)

/-- A completed transaction either commits a successful run or rolls back a
revert/panic. Waiting keeps the persistent data and can leave time unchanged. -/
inductive Step (M : System C D A) : World C → Event A → World C → Prop where
  | commit {s t : World C} {a : A} {tx : TTx}
      (accepted : s.accepts tx) (allowed : M.allowCall s a tx)
      (run : M.run s a tx = .ok t) : Step M s (.call a tx) t
  | rollback {s : World C} {a : A} {tx : TTx} {e : THalt}
      (accepted : s.accepts tx) (allowed : M.allowCall s a tx)
      (run : M.run s a tx = .error e)
      (failed : e = .revert ∨ (∃ data, e = .revertWith data) ∨ e = .panic) :
      Step M s (.call a tx) (s.atTime tx.timestamp)
  | wait {s : World C} {t : PrimTy.uint.Denote} (later : s.timestamp.1 ≤ t.1) :
      Step M s (.wait t) (s.atTime t)

/-- A finite, labelled execution. Every call link carries actual run evidence. -/
inductive Trace (M : System C D A) : World C → List (Event A) → World C → Prop where
  | nil (s : World C) : Trace M s [] s
  | cons {s t u : World C} {a : Event A} {as : List (Event A)}
      (step : Step M s a t) (rest : Trace M t as u) : Trace M s (a :: as) u

/-- Concatenate two checked executions. -/
theorem Trace.append {M : System C D A} {s t u : World C} {as bs : List (Event A)}
    (h : Trace M s as t) (k : Trace M t bs u) : Trace M s (as ++ bs) u :=
  match h with
  | .nil _ => k
  | .cons step rest => .cons step (rest.append k)

/-- Reachability is rooted at a successful constructor and closed only under
the explicit interface and waiting. -/
inductive Reachable (M : System C D A) : World C → Prop where
  | init {s : World C} (deployed : M.Init s) : Reachable M s
  | step {s t : World C} {a : Event A} (before : Reachable M s)
      (next : Step M s a t) : Reachable M t

/-- A finite continuation of a reached state remains reachable. -/
theorem Trace.reachable {M : System C D A} {s t : World C} {as : List (Event A)}
    (h : Trace M s as t) (hs : Reachable M s) : Reachable M t :=
  match h with
  | .nil _ => hs
  | .cons step rest => rest.reachable (.step hs step)

/-- Every reached state has a finite execution witness from deployment. -/
theorem Reachable.trace {M : System C D A} {t : World C} (h : Reachable M t) :
    ∃ s as, M.Init s ∧ Trace M s as t :=
  match h with
  | .init hs => ⟨_, [], hs, .nil _⟩
  | .step before next =>
    let ⟨s, as, hs, path⟩ := before.trace
    ⟨s, as ++ [_], hs, path.append (.cons next (.nil _))⟩

/-- Reachability and a finite deployment-rooted trace describe the same states. -/
theorem reachable_iff_trace {M : System C D A} {t : World C} :
    Reachable M t ↔ ∃ s as, M.Init s ∧ Trace M s as t :=
  ⟨Reachable.trace, fun ⟨_, _, hs, path⟩ => path.reachable (.init hs)⟩

/-- Always: the predicate holds at every state reachable after deployment. -/
def AG (M : System C D A) (P : World C → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ s, Reachable M s → P s

/-- Possible eventual reachability from a specified state, including zero steps. -/
def CanReach (M : System C D A) (s : World C) (P : World C → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ as t, Trace M s as t ∧ P t

/-- A target that holds now needs no transaction. -/
theorem CanReach.here {M : System C D A} {s : World C} {P : World C → Prop}
    (h : P s) : CanReach M s P := ⟨[], s, .nil s, h⟩

/-- Prepend an admitted action to a finite target witness. -/
theorem CanReach.next {M : System C D A} {s t : World C} {a : Event A}
    {P : World C → Prop} (step : Step M s a t) (h : CanReach M t P) : CanReach M s P :=
  let ⟨as, u, path, hu⟩ := h
  ⟨a :: as, u, .cons step path, hu⟩

/-- Possible eventually: some successful deployment has a finite target trace. -/
def EF (M : System C D A) (P : World C → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ s, M.Init s ∧ CanReach M s P

/-- From every reached state a target remains reachable; this does not require
any participant actually to take that continuation. -/
def AGEF (M : System C D A) (P : World C → Prop) : Prop :=
  AG M (fun s => CanReach M s P)

/-- Constructor establishment and preservation by every admitted transition. -/
structure Invariant (M : System C D A) (I : World C → Prop) : Prop where
  initially : ∀ s, M.Init s → I s
  preserved : ∀ {s t a}, I s → Step M s a t → I t

/-- An inductive invariant holds throughout the deployed contract's lifetime. -/
theorem Invariant.always {M : System C D A} {I : World C → Prop}
    (h : Invariant M I) : AG M I :=
  fun _ reached => go reached
where
  go {s : World C} (reached : Reachable M s) : I s :=
    match reached with
    | .init deployed => h.initially _ deployed
    | .step before next => h.preserved (go before) next

/-- Exclude a bad state using an invariant stronger than its negation. -/
theorem Invariant.never {M : System C D A} {I Bad : World C → Prop}
    (h : Invariant M I) (safe : ∀ s, I s → ¬ Bad s) : AG M (fun s => ¬ Bad s) :=
  fun s reached => safe s (h.always s reached)

/-- Establish an invariant from successful constructor/call runs and stability
under advancing time. Rollback needs no separate storage or payment proof. -/
theorem Invariant.ofRuns {M : System C D A} {I : World C → Prop}
    (deploy : ∀ d tx σ, M.allowDeploy d tx →
      C.deployT (M.deploy d) tx = .ok σ → I (World.ofState σ))
    (commit : ∀ s a tx t, s.accepts tx → M.allowCall s a tx → I s →
      M.run s a tx = .ok t → I t)
    (time : ∀ s t, s.timestamp.1 ≤ t.1 → I s → I (s.atTime t)) : Invariant M I where
  initially := fun _ ⟨d, tx, σ, allowed, run, eq⟩ => eq ▸ deploy d tx σ allowed run
  preserved := fun hi step => match step with
    | .commit accepted allowed run => commit _ _ _ _ accepted allowed hi run
    | .rollback accepted _ _ _ => time _ _ accepted.2.1 hi
    | .wait later => time _ _ later hi

/-- A target witness names a genuinely reached state. -/
theorem EF.reachable {M : System C D A} {P : World C → Prop} (h : EF M P) :
    ∃ t, Reachable M t ∧ P t :=
  let ⟨_, hs, _, t, path, ht⟩ := h
  ⟨t, path.reachable (.init hs), ht⟩

/-- Possible eventually is exactly a reachable target, not an exhausted run. -/
theorem ef_iff_reachable {M : System C D A} {P : World C → Prop} :
    EF M P ↔ ∃ t, Reachable M t ∧ P t :=
  ⟨EF.reachable, fun ⟨_, ht, hp⟩ =>
    let ⟨s, as, hs, path⟩ := ht.trace
    ⟨s, hs, as, _, path, hp⟩⟩

/-- A safety theorem rules out every finite witness to a bad state. -/
theorem AG.not_EF {M : System C D A} {P : World C → Prop}
    (h : AG M (fun s => ¬ P s)) : ¬ EF M P :=
  fun witness => let ⟨t, ht, hp⟩ := witness.reachable; h t ht hp

end Solidity.Lifetime

import Solidity.Semantics.Deploy

/-!
# Typed instances and atomic contract-world frames

This is an explicit execution interface, above the single-contract run. A
catalog indexes each instance's storage by its contract. Bodies and their
payable metadata are supplied by the model, as in Lifetime.System; this module
does not certify source lowering or replace the run's external-response table.

Fresh addresses are selected explicitly, checked for collision, and bounded
to 160 bits. All account balances are explicit. A frame commits storage and
settles the interpreter's net ledger only after successful execution. Failed
frames return no changed world. Creation catches enclose only the creation
frame, leaving argument evaluation and the successful continuation outside.

Linked library bodies are resolved at the caller's storage types and run with
the caller's identity, sender and value. The link's installed identity is
checked. Static frames conservatively accept empty-body observations only;
general computed view bodies require a future effect-certified interface.
-/

namespace Solidity.ContractWorld

abbrev Word := Semantics.Word

/-- An account address, bounded independently of the 256-bit value sort. -/
abbrev Address := { w : Word // w.1 < (2 : Int) ^ 160 }

/-- Refuse a word which cannot identify an account. -/
def Address.ofWord? (w : Word) : Option Address :=
  if h : w.1 < (2 : Int) ^ 160 then some ⟨w, h⟩ else none

/-- A typed contract reference is an address, not a proof of installed code.
As with a Solidity contract cast, every call still checks the actual catalog
identity. References can therefore survive a change of world. -/
structure Handle {K : Type} (k : K) where
  address : Address

/-- Code identity indexes the stored data; different contracts cannot share
an untyped storage object. -/
abbrev Account {K : Type} (contracts : K → Contract) :=
  (k : K) × Storage (contracts k)

/-- The source kind of installed code. It is fixed by the world's catalog. -/
inductive Role where
  | contractCode
  | libraryCode

/-- Global balances and typed per-instance persistent storage. Funding and
installed code in an initial world are explicit chain premises. -/
structure World {K : Type} (contracts : K → Contract) where
  accounts : Address → Option (Account contracts)
  funds : Address → Word
  timestamp : Word := PrimTy.dflt .uint
  roles : K → Role := fun _ => .contractCode

variable {K : Type} [DecidableEq K] {contracts : K → Contract}

/-- No deployed instances; externally supplied funding is still explicit. -/
def World.empty (contracts : K → Contract) (funds : Address → Word)
    (roles : K → Role := fun _ => .contractCode) : World contracts :=
  { accounts := fun _ => none, funds, roles }

/-- Library code is never an ordinary mutable contract entry. -/
def World.isLibrary (w : World contracts) (k : K) : Bool :=
  match w.roles k with
  | .contractCode => false
  | .libraryCode => true

/-- Arbitrary-address balance reads use the global account ledger. -/
def World.balance (w : World contracts) (a : Address) : Word := w.funds a

/-- Advance the common chain time between completed transactions. -/
def World.atTime (w : World contracts) (timestamp : Word) : World contracts :=
  { w with timestamp := timestamp }

/-- Read storage only after checking the instance's actual code identity. -/
def World.storage? (w : World contracts) {k : K} (r : Handle k) :
    Option (Storage (contracts k)) := do
  let ⟨j, st⟩ ← w.accounts r.address
  if h : j = k then some (h ▸ st) else none

/-- Sender, incoming value and explicitly assumed external responses.
Every frame in a world uses its common chain timestamp. -/
inductive Mode where
  | ordinary (payment : Word)
  | readOnly

/-- Read-only frames carry no payment, by construction. -/
structure Context where
  sender : Address
  mode : Mode := .ordinary (PrimTy.dflt .uint)
  ext : List (Semantics.ExtKey × Semantics.ExtResult) := []

/-- The incoming value retained by an ordinary or delegated frame. -/
def Context.value (ctx : Context) : Word :=
  match ctx.mode with
  | .ordinary value => value
  | .readOnly => PrimTy.dflt .uint

/-- Whether this frame inherits the static restriction. -/
def Context.isStatic (ctx : Context) : Bool :=
  match ctx.mode with
  | .ordinary _ => false
  | .readOnly => true

/-- Construct the actual typed transaction seen by the body. -/
def Context.tx (ctx : Context) (w : World contracts) (self : Address) : TTx :=
  { msgSender := ctx.sender.1, selfAddress := self.1, msgValue := ctx.value,
    timestamp := w.timestamp, ext := ctx.ext }

/-- Static observations can decode a value without executing a statement.
Nonempty programs are refused in static mode rather than assuming that their
final state equality proves the absence of attempted writes. -/
def emptyBody {C : Contract} {Γ Δ : Ctx} : Prog C Γ Δ → Bool
  | .nil => true
  | .cons _ _ => false

/-- An explicitly resolved entry, retaining the types of all result locals.
The decoder belongs to the caller and may fail after the frame succeeds. -/
structure Entry (C : Contract) (α : Type) where
  locals : Ctx
  body : Prog C [] locals
  result : State C locals → TRes α
  payable : Bool := false

/-- A closed method whose result is discarded. -/
def Entry.unit {C : Contract} (P : Prog C [] []) (payable : Bool := false) : Entry C Unit :=
  ⟨[], P, fun _ => .ok (), payable⟩

/-- A fresh paid frame. Self-calls still require funding but move no funds.
The ledger starts empty except for this frame's incoming payment. -/
def World.enter (w : World contracts) {k : K} (self : Address) (ctx : Context)
    (st : Storage (contracts k)) (payable : Bool) : TRes (State (contracts k) []) := do
  if ctx.value.1 > (w.funds ctx.sender).1 then .error .revert else do
    if (!payable || ctx.isStatic) && ctx.value.1 != 0 then .error .revert else do
      let balance ← TRes.ofOpt (PrimTy.ofInt? .uint
        ((w.funds self).1 + if ctx.sender = self then 0 else ctx.value.1))
      pure {
        storage := st, H := [], heap := Heap.empty, env := (), selfBalance := balance,
        net := if ctx.sender = self ∨ ctx.value.1 = 0 then [] else [(ctx.sender.1, ctx.value.1)],
        tx := ctx.tx w self }

/-- Apply the frame's finite net ledger to other accounts. A positive net
entry is a payment into the frame; a negative one is a receipt by that
account. The frame's own balance has already been computed by the run.
Repeated keys use the ledger's first-entry convention. Invalid address keys, unfunded debits and overflowing credits fail closed. -/
def settle (funds : Address → Word) (self : Address) (net : Ledger) : TRes (Address → Word) :=
  go funds [] net
where
  go (funds : Address → Word) (seen : List Word) : Ledger → TRes (Address → Word)
    | [] => .ok funds
    | (a, n) :: rest =>
      if a ∈ seen ∨ a = self.1 then go funds (a :: seen) rest else do
        let address ← TRes.ofOpt (Address.ofWord? a)
        let balance ← TRes.ofOpt (PrimTy.ofInt? .uint ((funds address).1 - n))
        go (fun b => if b = address then balance else funds b) (a :: seen) rest

/-- Commit one successful frame, updating exactly its own typed storage.
Settlement cannot modify code or any other instance's storage: its result
type contains balances alone. -/
def World.finish (w : World contracts) {k : K} {Γ : Ctx} (self : Address)
    (σ : State (contracts k) Γ) : TRes (World contracts) := do
  let funds ← settle w.funds self σ.net
  pure { w with
    accounts := fun a => if a = self then some ⟨k, σ.storage⟩ else w.accounts a,
    funds := fun a => if a = self then σ.selfBalance else funds a }

/-- A commit's code/storage map changes only at the executing instance. -/
theorem World.finish_accounts {w t : World contracts} {k : K} {Γ : Ctx}
    {self : Address} {σ : State (contracts k) Γ} (run : w.finish self σ = .ok t) :
    t.accounts = fun a => if a = self then some ⟨k, σ.storage⟩ else w.accounts a := by
  unfold World.finish at run
  cases hs : settle w.funds self σ.net with
  | error e => simp only [hs, bind, Except.bind] at run; cases run
  | ok funds =>
    simp only [hs, bind, Except.bind] at run
    cases run
    rfl

/-- Independently addressed instances retain their storage after a commit. -/
theorem World.finish_other {w t : World contracts} {k : K} {Γ : Ctx}
    {self a : Address} {σ : State (contracts k) Γ} (run : w.finish self σ = .ok t)
    (different : a ≠ self) : t.accounts a = w.accounts a := by
  rw [World.finish_accounts run]
  exact if_neg different

/-- Ordinary creation: collision/funding checks, fresh initial storage,
constructor execution and payment settlement, followed by code installation.
The supplied closed body must include the source's base/field initializers. -/
private def World.deployFrame (w : World contracts) (k : K) (self : Address)
    (ctor : Prog (contracts k) [] []) (ctx : Context) :
    TRes (World contracts × Handle k) := do
  if (w.accounts self).isSome || decide (self = ctx.sender) || ctx.isStatic then .error .revert else do
    let σ ← w.enter self ctx (Storage.init (contracts k))
      (((contracts k).ctor.map (·.payable)).getD false)
    let o ← ctor.run σ
    let next ← w.finish self o.st
    pure (next, ⟨self⟩)

/-- Ordinary source creation cannot instantiate a library declaration. -/
def World.create (w : World contracts) (k : K) (self : Address)
    (ctor : Prog (contracts k) [] []) (ctx : Context) :
    TRes (World contracts × Handle k) :=
  if w.isLibrary k then .error .revert else w.deployFrame k self ctor ctx

/-- Deploy library code for a linked identity. Its implicit deployment cannot
have mutable fields, initializers or a user constructor. This is deployment
of a library declaration, not source-level new L(). -/
def World.deployLibrary (w : World contracts) (k : K) (self : Address) (ctx : Context) :
    TRes (World contracts × Handle k) :=
  if !w.isLibrary k || !(contracts k).vars.isEmpty || (contracts k).ctor.isSome ||
      !(contracts k).inits.isEmpty then .error .revert
  else w.deployFrame k self .nil ctx

/-- Execute the actual callee body against that instance's storage. -/
def World.callFrame (w : World contracts) {k : K} {α : Type} (r : Handle k)
    (entry : Entry (contracts k) α) (ctx : Context) :
    TRes (World contracts × State (contracts k) entry.locals) := do
  if w.isLibrary k || (ctx.isStatic && !(emptyBody entry.body)) then .error .revert else do
    let st ← TRes.ofOpt (w.storage? r)
    let σ ← w.enter r.address ctx st entry.payable
    let o ← entry.body.run σ
    let next ← w.finish r.address o.st
    pure (next, o.st)

/-- Every successful call frame contains an actual successful typed run,
with its paid entry and exact settlement exposed for correctness bridges. -/
theorem World.callFrame_ok {w next : World contracts} {k : K} {α : Type}
    {r : Handle k} {entry : Entry (contracts k) α} {ctx : Context}
    {result : State (contracts k) entry.locals}
    (run : w.callFrame r entry ctx = .ok (next, result)) :
    ∃ (st : Storage (contracts k)) (σ : State (contracts k) [])
      (o : Out (contracts k) σ.H entry.locals),
      w.storage? r = some st ∧ w.enter r.address ctx st entry.payable = .ok σ ∧
      entry.body.run σ = .ok o ∧ w.finish r.address o.st = .ok next ∧ o.st = result := by
  unfold World.callFrame at run
  split at run
  · cases run
  · cases hs : w.storage? r with
    | none => simp only [hs, TRes.ofOpt, bind, Except.bind] at run; cases run
    | some st =>
      simp only [hs, TRes.ofOpt, bind, Except.bind] at run
      cases he : w.enter r.address ctx st entry.payable with
      | error e => simp only [he, bind, Except.bind] at run; cases run
      | ok σ =>
        simp only [he, bind, Except.bind] at run
        cases hr : entry.body.run σ with
        | error e => simp only [hr] at run; cases run
        | ok o =>
          simp only [hr] at run
          cases hf : w.finish r.address o.st with
          | error e => simp only [hf, bind, Except.bind] at run; cases run
          | ok final =>
            simp only [hf, bind, Except.bind] at run
            have eq : (final, o.st) = (next, result) := Except.ok.inj run
            exact ⟨st, σ, o, rfl, he, hr,
              hf.trans (congrArg (fun x => Except.ok x) (congrArg Prod.fst eq)),
              congrArg Prod.snd eq⟩

/-- Creation success witnesses the constructor run from fresh typed storage,
not merely an oracle reply or a default deployed account. -/
private theorem World.deployFrame_ok {w next : World contracts} {k : K} {self : Address}
    {ctor : Prog (contracts k) [] []} {ctx : Context} {reference : Handle k}
    (run : w.deployFrame k self ctor ctx = .ok (next, reference)) :
    ∃ (σ : State (contracts k) []) (o : Out (contracts k) σ.H []),
      w.enter self ctx (Storage.init (contracts k))
        (((contracts k).ctor.map (·.payable)).getD false) = .ok σ ∧
      ctor.run σ = .ok o ∧ w.finish self o.st = .ok next ∧ reference.address = self := by
  unfold World.deployFrame at run
  split at run
  · cases run
  · cases he : w.enter self ctx (Storage.init (contracts k))
        (((contracts k).ctor.map (·.payable)).getD false) with
    | error e => simp only [he, bind, Except.bind] at run; cases run
    | ok σ =>
      simp only [he, bind, Except.bind] at run
      cases hr : ctor.run σ with
      | error e => simp only [hr] at run; cases run
      | ok o =>
        simp only [hr] at run
        cases hf : w.finish self o.st with
        | error e => simp only [hf, bind, Except.bind] at run; cases run
        | ok final =>
          simp only [hf, bind, Except.bind] at run
          have eq : (final, (⟨self⟩ : Handle k)) = (next, reference) := Except.ok.inj run
          exact ⟨σ, o, rfl, hr,
            hf.trans (congrArg (fun x => Except.ok x) (congrArg Prod.fst eq)),
            (congrArg Handle.address (congrArg Prod.snd eq)).symm⟩

/-- Successful ordinary creation retains the actual constructor witness. -/
theorem World.create_ok {w next : World contracts} {k : K} {self : Address}
    {ctor : Prog (contracts k) [] []} {ctx : Context} {reference : Handle k}
    (run : w.create k self ctor ctx = .ok (next, reference)) :
    ∃ (σ : State (contracts k) []) (o : Out (contracts k) σ.H []),
      w.enter self ctx (Storage.init (contracts k))
        (((contracts k).ctor.map (·.payable)).getD false) = .ok σ ∧
      ctor.run σ = .ok o ∧ w.finish self o.st = .ok next ∧ reference.address = self := by
  unfold World.create at run
  split at run
  · cases run
  · exact World.deployFrame_ok run

/-- A successful constructor installs its own storage at its own code type. -/
theorem World.create_installs {w next : World contracts} {k : K} {self : Address}
    {ctor : Prog (contracts k) [] []} {ctx : Context} {reference : Handle k}
    (run : w.create k self ctor ctx = .ok (next, reference)) :
    ∃ st : Storage (contracts k), next.accounts reference.address = some ⟨k, st⟩ := by
  obtain ⟨σ, o, _, _, finish, address⟩ := World.create_ok run
  refine ⟨o.st.storage, ?_⟩
  rw [address, World.finish_accounts finish]
  exact if_pos rfl

/-- Caller-side return decoding happens after the callee's frame. Its failure
propagates; this operation contains no catch around the decoder. -/
def World.call (w : World contracts) {k : K} {α : Type} (r : Handle k)
    (entry : Entry (contracts k) α) (ctx : Context) : TRes (World contracts × α) := do
  let (next, σ) ← w.callFrame r entry ctx
  let result ← entry.result σ
  pure (next, result)

/-- An installed library identity and its body resolved at the caller's types.
Declaration-aware resolution and storage-parameter mapping are model
obligations, not consequences of matching an arbitrary address. -/
structure Library (contracts : K → Contract) (caller : K) (α : Type) where
  kind : K
  address : Address
  entry : Entry (contracts caller) α

/-- A linked body uses caller storage and identity, preserving the original
sender and value without charging an additional incoming payment. The
library's own storage and funds are never substituted for the caller's. -/
def World.libraryCall (w : World contracts) {caller : K} {α : Type}
    (r : Handle caller) (library : Library contracts caller α) (ctx : Context) :
    TRes (World contracts × α) := do
  if !w.isLibrary library.kind || w.isLibrary caller ||
      (ctx.isStatic && !(emptyBody library.entry.body)) then .error .revert else do
    let _ ← TRes.ofOpt (w.storage? (⟨library.address⟩ : Handle library.kind))
    let st ← TRes.ofOpt (w.storage? r)
    let σ : State (contracts caller) [] := {
      storage := st, H := [], heap := Heap.empty, env := (), net := [],
      selfBalance := w.funds r.address, tx := ctx.tx w r.address }
    let o ← library.entry.body.run σ
    let next ← w.finish r.address o.st
    let result ← library.entry.result o.st
    pure (next, result)

/-- Exactly the halts which a completed creation-frame catch can observe.
Mathematical divergence and model exhaustion do not become caught reverts. -/
def catchable : THalt → Bool
  | .revert | .revertWith _ | .panic => true
  | .diverge | .exhausted => false

/-- Run arguments before entering the catch boundary. Only the creation
frame is caught; a failure in either continuation propagates unchanged. -/
def World.tryCreate {α β : Type} (w : World contracts) (args : TRes α) (k : K)
    (target : α → Address) (ctor : α → Prog (contracts k) [] [])
    (context : α → Context)
    (success : World contracts → Handle k → TRes (World contracts × β))
    (caught : World contracts → THalt → TRes (World contracts × β)) :
    TRes (World contracts × β) := do
  let a ← args
  let ctx := context a
  if ctx.isStatic then .error .revert else
    match w.create k (target a) (ctor a) ctx with
    | .ok (next, reference) => success next reference
    | .error e => if catchable e then caught w e else .error e

/-- No constructor handler can intercept argument evaluation failures. -/
theorem World.tryCreate_argument_failure {α β : Type} (w : World contracts) (e : THalt)
    (k : K) (target : α → Address) (ctor : α → Prog (contracts k) [] [])
    (context : α → Context)
    (success : World contracts → Handle k → TRes (World contracts × β))
    (caught : World contracts → THalt → TRes (World contracts × β)) :
    w.tryCreate (.error e) k target ctor context success caught = .error e := rfl

/-- At a transaction boundary, a failure exposes exactly the original world.
Use completed-failure evidence separately when deriving a chain transition. -/
def atomic {α : Type} (w : World contracts)
    (run : TRes (World contracts × α)) : World contracts × TRes α :=
  match run with
  | .ok (next, result) => (next, .ok result)
  | .error e => (w, .error e)

/-- All writes and payments are rolled back together on failure. -/
theorem atomic_failure {α : Type} (w : World contracts) (e : THalt) :
    atomic w (.error e : TRes (World contracts × α)) = (w, .error e) := rfl

/-- Actual world operations, including an atomic sequence. Bodies still have
the explicit interface obligations of Entry and Library. -/
inductive Operation (contracts : K → Contract) where
  | create (k : K) (self : Address) (body : Prog (contracts k) [] []) (ctx : Context)
  | deployLibrary (k : K) (self : Address) (ctx : Context)
  | call (k : K) (reference : Handle k) (entry : Entry (contracts k) Unit) (ctx : Context)
  | libraryCall (k : K) (reference : Handle k) (library : Library contracts k Unit) (ctx : Context)
  | seq (first second : Operation contracts)

/-- Each operation runs the checked world frames; sequences expose no
intermediate world if their second operation fails. -/
def Operation.run : Operation contracts → World contracts → TRes (World contracts)
  | .create k self body ctx, w => do
    let (next, _) ← w.create k self body ctx
    pure next
  | .deployLibrary k self ctx, w => do
    let (next, _) ← w.deployLibrary k self ctx
    pure next
  | .call _ reference entry ctx, w => do
    let (next, _) ← w.call reference entry ctx
    pure next
  | .libraryCall _ reference library ctx, w => do
    let (next, _) ← w.libraryCall reference library ctx
    pure next
  | .seq first second, w => do
    let next ← first.run w
    second.run next

/-- A completed world transaction, with explicit chain/environment premises.
Rollback requires a completed failure; exhaustion never supplies a step. -/
inductive Step (allowed : World contracts → Operation contracts → Prop) :
    World contracts → World contracts → Prop where
  | commit {w next : World contracts} {op : Operation contracts}
      (admitted : allowed w op) (run : op.run w = .ok next) : Step allowed w next
  | rollback {w : World contracts} {op : Operation contracts} {e : THalt}
      (admitted : allowed w op) (run : op.run w = .error e)
      (completed : catchable e = true) : Step allowed w w
  | wait {w : World contracts} {timestamp : Word}
      (later : w.timestamp.1 ≤ timestamp.1) : Step allowed w (w.atTime timestamp)

/-- Starting with funded accounts and no code, every deployed instance is
introduced by a successful constructor frame, possibly within a sequence. -/
inductive Reachable (funding : Address → Word) (roles : K → Role)
    (allowed : World contracts → Operation contracts → Prop) : World contracts → Prop where
  | initial : Reachable funding roles allowed (World.empty contracts funding roles)
  | step {w next : World contracts} (before : Reachable funding roles allowed w)
      (run : Step allowed w next) : Reachable funding roles allowed next

/-- Transaction-reachable safety is distinct from validity on arbitrary typed
states. All constructor, call, linking and environment obligations are visible
in the transition premise. -/
theorem reachable_invariant {funding : Address → Word} {roles : K → Role}
    {allowed : World contracts → Operation contracts → Prop} {I : World contracts → Prop}
    (initial : I (World.empty contracts funding roles))
    (preserved : ∀ {w next}, I w → Step allowed w next → I next)
    {w : World contracts} (reached : Reachable funding roles allowed w) : I w := by
  induction reached with
  | initial => exact initial
  | step _ run ih => exact preserved ih run

end Solidity.ContractWorld

import Solidity.Semantics.Run

/-!
# The deployment, typed

A deployment runs `constructor(args);` from the state a contract starts in
when it is created, after the creation code's `CALLVALUE` check.  Here, over
the typed run alone, so that `#deploy` (`Tools/Run.lean`) runs exactly what
the constructor obligation is read at (`Calculus/Deploy.lean`), without
importing the calculus.
-/

namespace Solidity

variable {C : Contract}

/-- The state a deployment starts in: the
empty storage, no memory, a ledger holding the deployer's payment, and the
value sent as the contract's funds. -/
def State.deploy (C : Contract) (tx : TTx) : State C [] :=
  { storage := Storage.init C, H := [], heap := Heap.empty, env := (),
    net := [(tx.msgSender, tx.msgValue.1)], selfBalance := tx.msgValue, tx := tx }

/-- **The typed deployment** (master's `Contract.deploy`, over the typed run): a
constructor that is not `payable`, the implicit one too, refuses value, as
solc's creation code does; otherwise its program runs from
`State.deploy`. -/
def Contract.deployT (C : Contract) {Γ' : Ctx} (P : Prog C [] Γ') (tx : TTx) :
    TRes (State C Γ') :=
  if !((C.ctor.map (·.payable)).getD false) && tx.msgValue.1 != 0 then .error .revert
  else do
    let o ← Prog.run (State.deploy C tx) P
    pure o.st

end Solidity
