import Solidity.Semantics.Heap

/-!
# The typed state

A local holds a value of its type (`LTy.TDenote`), an alias a typed storage
reference, a memory local a reference its heap typing types; the state
holds a typed storage and a heap whose typing `H` is a field, not an index,
so a statement's run keeps its type.  An allocation grows the heap
(`State.adopt`, from a `Grown` heap) and weakens the locals along the
extension (`TEnv.wk`), which only rewrites a memory local's proof: the
identities stay.

The terms read the typed state itself (`Signature.lean`, W9.8), and so do
the run's invariants (`Typing/`), the EVM simulation (`Evm/Sim.lean`) and
the tools: there is no untyped state (W10.5.6).
-/

namespace Solidity

variable {C : Contract}

/-! ## Locals -/

/-- What a local of type `t` holds, typed: a value of its type, the storage
reference an alias is bound to (`none` while unset), a memory reference the
heap typing `H` types (`none` while unset: no statement leaves one so, only
a hidden binder ranges over it, decision 17'), a whole storage, a ledger. -/
@[reducible] def LTy.TDenote (C : Contract) (H : HTy) : LTy → Type
  | .val p => p.Denote
  | .alias R => Option (SRef C (.ref R))
  | .mem R => Option (HRef H R)
  | .old => Storage C
  | .oldNet => Ledger
  | .kint => Int

namespace LTy

/-- A local over a grown heap: a memory reference weakened, the rest kept. -/
def TDenote.wk {H H' : HTy} (e : H <+: H') : (t : LTy) → t.TDenote C H → t.TDenote C H'
  | .val _, v => v
  | .alias _, a => a
  | .mem _, r => r.map (HRef.wk e)
  | .old, st => st
  | .oldNet, l => l
  | .kint, n => n

end LTy

/-- The locals of `Γ`, typed over the heap typing `H`: computed from `Γ`, as
a type computed from the context, not an inductive family (Gate G0, condition 4). -/
def TEnv (C : Contract) (H : HTy) : Ctx → Type
  | [] => Unit
  | t :: Γ => t.TDenote C H × TEnv C H Γ

namespace TEnv

variable {H : HTy}

/-- The local at a position. -/
def get : {Γ : Ctx} → {t : LTy} → Idx Γ t → TEnv C H Γ → t.TDenote C H
  | _, _, i => Idx.casesOn (motive := fun Γ t _ => TEnv C H Γ → t.TDenote C H) i
      (fun e => e.1) (fun i e => TEnv.get i e.2)
  termination_by structural _ _ i => i

/-- The local at a position, set. -/
def set : {Γ : Ctx} → {t : LTy} → Idx Γ t → t.TDenote C H → TEnv C H Γ → TEnv C H Γ
  | _, _, i => Idx.casesOn (motive := fun Γ t _ => t.TDenote C H → TEnv C H Γ → TEnv C H Γ) i
      (fun w e => (w, e.2)) (fun i w e => (e.1, TEnv.set i w e.2))
  termination_by structural _ _ i => i

/-- The locals a suffix pushed, popped. -/
def drop {Γ : Ctx} : {Δ : Ctx} → Ext Γ Δ → TEnv C H Δ → TEnv C H Γ
  | _, h => Ext.casesOn (motive := fun Δ _ => TEnv C H Δ → TEnv C H Γ) h (fun e => e)
      (fun h e => TEnv.drop h e.2)
  termination_by structural _ h => h

/-- The locals over a grown heap. -/
def wk {H' : HTy} (e : H <+: H') : (Γ : Ctx) → TEnv C H Γ → TEnv C H' Γ
  | [], _ => ()
  | t :: Γ, x => (LTy.TDenote.wk e t x.1, TEnv.wk e Γ x.2)

theorem get_wk {H' : HTy} (e : H <+: H') {t : LTy} : {Γ : Ctx} → (i : Idx Γ t) →
    (x : TEnv C H Γ) → TEnv.get i (TEnv.wk e Γ x) = LTy.TDenote.wk e t (TEnv.get i x)
  | _, .here, _ => rfl
  | _, .there i, x => get_wk e i x.2

end TEnv

/-! ## States -/

/-- The transaction: KeY's program variables `msgSender` and `msgValue`
(`netHeader.key`), the contract's own address and the block's timestamp,
`uint`s, so in range by construction; and how each external call it makes
ends (`ext`), a call it has no entry for reaching an address with no code
(which a `try` reverts on, and a `send` pays: `sendT`).  Two identical
calls, or two `send`s of one amount to one address, read the same entry.
No statement changes them, and a callback leaves them as they were: a
re-entrant call runs in its own transaction, which the caller never sees.
The outcomes are ABI data (`Semantics.ExtResult`), read back at their types
when a `try` decodes them.  The calculus reads none of `ext`: a `try` has a
goal for every way its call may end (`tryCallNoCallbackBox`), a `send` one
for each outcome (`sendNoCallbackBox`), so a proof holds whatever the table
says. -/
structure TTx where
  msgSender : PrimTy.uint.Denote := PrimTy.dflt .uint
  selfAddress : PrimTy.uint.Denote := PrimTy.dflt .uint
  msgValue : PrimTy.uint.Denote := PrimTy.dflt .uint
  timestamp : PrimTy.uint.Denote := PrimTy.dflt .uint
  ext : List (Semantics.ExtKey × Semantics.ExtResult) := []

/-- A state in the context `Γ`, typed: the storage at the contract's
types, a heap and its typing, the locals typed over it, the contract's own
funds a `uint` (no statement changes them: a payment moves the ledger). -/
structure State (C : Contract) (Γ : Ctx) where
  storage : Storage C
  H : HTy
  heap : Heap H
  env : TEnv C H Γ
  net : Ledger := []
  selfBalance : PrimTy.uint.Denote := PrimTy.dflt .uint
  tx : TTx := {}

namespace State

variable {Γ : Ctx}

/-- The state a contract starts in: every state variable at its default, no
memory, no locals. -/
def init (C : Contract) : State C [] :=
  { storage := Storage.init C, H := [], heap := Heap.empty, env := () }

/-- A local declared. -/
def push {t : LTy} (σ : State C Γ) (v : t.TDenote C σ.H) : State C (t :: Γ) :=
  { σ with env := (v, σ.env) }

/-- A local set. -/
def setLocal {t : LTy} (σ : State C Γ) (i : Idx Γ t) (v : t.TDenote C σ.H) : State C Γ :=
  { σ with env := TEnv.set i v σ.env }

/-- A scope's locals popped. -/
def drop {Δ : Ctx} (h : Ext Γ Δ) (σ : State C Δ) : State C Γ :=
  { σ with env := TEnv.drop h σ.env }

/-- The global part of a typed state: the state without its locals. -/
def glob (σ : State C Γ) : State C [] :=
  { storage := σ.storage, H := σ.H, heap := σ.heap, env := (), net := σ.net,
    selfBalance := σ.selfBalance, tx := σ.tx }

/-- The storage replaced. -/
def withStorage (σ : State C Γ) (st : Storage C) : State C Γ := { σ with storage := st }

/-- A new external transaction resets transient cells and memory. Internal
calls and caught failures never use this boundary operation. -/
def transactionEntry (σ : State C []) : State C [] :=
  { storage := Storage.resetTransient σ.storage, H := [], heap := Heap.empty,
    env := (), net := σ.net, selfBalance := σ.selfBalance, tx := σ.tx }

/-! ### Allocation -/

/-- A grown heap adopted: its typing and objects, the locals weakened along
its extension, and the value it carries, typed over the new typing. -/
def adopt {α : HTy → Type} (σ : State C Γ) (g : Grown σ.H α) :
    (σ' : State C Γ) × α σ'.H :=
  ⟨{ σ with H := g.H', heap := g.heap, env := TEnv.wk g.ext Γ σ.env }, g.val⟩

/-- A fresh object (`State.alloc`): the heap grows by its type. -/
def alloc {R : RefTy} (σ : State C Γ) (o : MObj σ.H R) :
    (σ' : State C Γ) × MVal σ'.H (.ref R) :=
  σ.adopt (Grown.alloc ⟨List.prefix_refl _, σ.heap, o⟩)

/-- A storage value copied into fresh objects (`copyStToM`). -/
def copyStToM {T : Ty} (σ : State C Γ) (v : SVal T) (h : T.mapFree = true) :
    (σ' : State C Γ) × MVal σ'.H T :=
  σ.adopt (v.copyStToM σ.heap h)

/-- A fresh default object (`allocDefault`). -/
def allocDefault (σ : State C Γ) (R : RefTy) (h : (Ty.ref R).mapFree = true) :
    (σ' : State C Γ) × MVal σ'.H (.ref R) :=
  σ.adopt (σ.heap.allocDefault R h)

/-- A memory value copied to storage (`copyMem`). -/
def copyMToSt {T : Ty} (σ : State C Γ) (v : MVal σ.H T) : SVal T := MVal.copyMToSt σ.heap v

/-- A fresh `Person` in memory: its members' objects first, then its own,
so the heap typing grows by three; its `age` reads its default.  By the
kernel: the copy is a fold. -/
example : (let g := (State.init StandardExample).allocDefault (.struct "Person") rfl
    (g.1.H.length, (g.1.heap.field g.2 (f := "age") rfl : PrimTy.uint.Denote).1)) =
    (3, 0) := by
  decide +kernel

end State

end Solidity

import Lean
import Solidity.Frontend.SolcJson
import Solidity.Syntax.Splice

/-!
# `solc_import`: a contract from solc's AST, at elaboration time

`solc_import "f.ast.json" hash 0x… as N renaming Triple => FixedTriple`
reads a fixture of `scripts/solc-ast.mjs` (the path is relative to the
importing file) and defines

* `N : Contract`, the contract's state variables and the functions called
  by name through `contract!{ … }`, each function checked alone first;
* `N.f : Prog N Γ Γ'` for each function `f` that elaborates, its body read
  against `N` with its parameters as locals in scope (`Γ`, newest first:
  `paramCtx`), after its return variables declared at their defaults, its
  loops and then its `return`s lowered (`lowerLoops`, `lowerReturns`), as a
  call inlines it;
* `N.constructor : Prog N Γ Γ'` for a declared constructor, a deployment:
  `constructor(x̄);` with its parameters as locals in scope (`elabCtor`).
  The contract declares the constructor (its member last, since it may
  call every function) and the state variables' initializers
  (`SolcContract.initMembers`) only if it expands with both, else neither:
  an implicit constructor's initializers left out are a warning, a declared
  one's a row;
* `N.report : List ImportRow`, one row per function, the constructor's
  first: its solkey tag
  (`tagOf`: which obligation solkey states, if any) and parameters, what
  became of it and why, with the source line.  A function whose obligation
  is a specification's, or that has none (`internal`), is still a program:
  only its plain statement is not made (`solc_scoped_problems`).

Each body is printed as `sol` text (`SolcJson.lean`), parsed as
`sol_raw!{ … }` and elaborated to a `List RawStmt` term by the macros, the
one lowering path `sol[C]{ … }` takes.  Those terms and the contract are
then evaluated together, one `evalExpr`, and the typed elaborator runs on
each as ordinary compiled code (`elabProgAtS.go`); `sol[C]{ … }` would
compile one program per function.  Its result, the scoped program, is
quoted back hash-consed with every proof `Eq.refl` (`Prog.quoteShared`,
`Prog.define`), so the kernel re-checks what it computed: every local the
program reads is in scope, at its type.  The programs are not compiled
(about half the import's time for the TestSuite): what evaluates one reads
its value (`#solc_show N.f`; an obligation, `Frontend/Problems.lean`).

Lake does not track the fixture, so the command names its hash (FNV-1a 64
over the bytes) and refuses a fixture of another one; the script that
writes the fixture rewrites the literal, which makes Lake re-check the
importing module.

A function that does not elaborate is a row, not an error: the import
never fails on one function.  Each body's elaboration has its own
heartbeats and catches runtime exceptions too (`tryCatchRuntimeEx`), so a
body that exhausts its budget is a row as well.  A row is found by its
index, not its name. Overloaded declarations have distinct internal names;
the reader refuses an unmangled function named `report` before any constant is made.
-/

namespace Solidity.Frontend

open Lean Elab Command Term Meta

/-- What the import made of a function. -/
inductive ImportStatus where
  /-- A constant `N.f : Prog N Γ Γ'`. -/
  | elaborated
  /-- solkey's `@custom:key skip`: no obligation. -/
  | skipped
  /-- The model has no counterpart (`Gap.excluded`). -/
  | excluded
  /-- The printer, the grammar or the typed elaborator lacks the form. -/
  | unsupported
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

def ImportStatus.toStr : ImportStatus → String
  | .elaborated => "elaborated"
  | .skipped => "skipped"
  | .excluded => "excluded"
  | .unsupported => "unsupported"

/-- A function of the imported contract and what became of it; `reason` is
`file:line: …`. -/
structure ImportRow where
  name : String
  /-- The Solidity name; `name` identifies the generated Lean declaration. -/
  sourceName : String := ""
  sourceSignature : String := ""
  /-- Exact solc declaration identity; -1 for a synthesized declaration. -/
  sourceId : Int := -1
  /-- Modern fixtures undergo the source scan; legacy fixtures do not. -/
  admissionChecked : Bool := false
  sourceFeatures : List Language.Feature := []
  sourceDiagnostic : Option Source.Diagnostic := none
  tag : Tag
  params : List (String × String)
  /-- Elaborated parameter types, newest first, including reference locations. -/
  paramTypes : Ctx := []
  status : ImportStatus
  reason : String
  /-- Declared `payable`. -/
  payable : Bool := false
  /-- It may call a callee that writes the state (`SolcFun.writingCall`). -/
  writingCall : Bool := true
  /-- The parameters the ABI decoder bounds (`SolcFun.paramRanges`). -/
  paramRanges : List (String × Int × Int) := []
  /-- The memory array parameters whose elements it bounds (`SolcFun.elemRanges`). -/
  elemRanges : List (String × Int × Int × Option Nat) := []
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

deriving instance ToExpr for Tag
deriving instance ToExpr for ImportStatus
deriving instance ToExpr for ImportRow

/-- The row of an imported function. -/
def ImportRow.ofFun (f : SolcFun) (status : ImportStatus) (reason : String) : ImportRow :=
  { name := f.name, sourceName := f.sourceName, sourceSignature := f.sourceSignature,
    sourceId := f.sourceId,
    sourceFeatures := f.sourceScope.features, sourceDiagnostic := f.sourceScope.diagnostic?,
    tag := f.tag, params := f.params, status, reason, payable := f.payable,
    writingCall := f.writingCall, paramRanges := f.paramRanges, elemRanges := f.elemRanges }

/-- The declaration `N.f` of the row `f` of `N`'s import. -/
def ImportRow.declName (N : Lean.Name) (r : ImportRow) : Lean.Name := N ++ Lean.Name.mkSimple r.name

/-- The counts by status, then every row that did not elaborate. -/
def ImportRow.summary (rows : List ImportRow) : String :=
  let count (s : ImportStatus) := (rows.filter (·.status == s)).length
  let tags := ", ".intercalate <| [Tag.diamond, .box, .skip, .specified, .internal, .malformed]
    |>.filterMap fun t =>
      let n := (rows.filter (·.tag == t)).length
      if n == 0 && t != .diamond && t != .box && t != .skip then none
      else some s!"{n} {t.toStr}"
  let head := s!"{rows.length} functions ({tags}): {count .elaborated} elaborated, \
    {count .skipped} skipped, {count .excluded} excluded, {count .unsupported} unsupported"
  let rest := rows.filter (·.status != .elaborated) |>.map fun r =>
    s!"{r.status.toStr} {r.name}: {r.reason}"
  "\n".intercalate (head :: rest)

/-- FNV-1a 64 over the bytes, `scripts/solc-ast.mjs`'s `hash`. -/
def fnv1a64 (b : ByteArray) : UInt64 :=
  b.foldl (fun h x => (h ^^^ x.toUInt64) * 0x100000001b3) 0xcbf29ce484222325

/-- `0x` and 16 hex digits, as `scripts/solc-ast.mjs` writes the hash. -/
def hex16 (h : UInt64) : String :=
  let d := (Nat.toDigits 16 h.toNat).asString
  "0x" ++ "".pushn '0' (16 - d.length) ++ d

/-- Every position of `stx` moved to `ref`'s, so a parsed text never
points into a string the file does not have. -/
partial def atRef (ref : Syntax) (stx : Syntax) : Syntax :=
  let info := SourceInfo.fromRef ref
  match stx with
  | .node _ k args => .node info k (args.map (atRef ref))
  | .atom _ v => .atom info v
  | .ident _ raw v pre => .ident info raw v pre
  | .missing => .missing

/-- The parameters of a function as locals in scope, most recent first. -/
def paramCtx (C : Contract) (ps : List RawStmt) : Except String ECtx :=
  ps.reverse.mapM fun s => match s with
    | .decl T x none => do
      let (.prim p, n) ← elabDeclTy C T | throw s!"reference parameter {x} needs a data location"
      -- a `bytesN` one with its marker (`bytesRowsOf`)
      pure (x, .val p n (← bytesRowsOf C T))
    | .declStorage T x none => do
      let (.ref R, ws) ← elabTyW C T | throw s!"storage location on value parameter {x}"
      pure (x, .alias R ws)
    | .declMemory T x none => do
      let (.ref R, ws) ← elabTyW C T | throw s!"memory location on value parameter {x}"
      unless (Ty.ref R).mapFree do throw s!"memory parameter {x} holds a mapping"
      pure (x, .mem R ws)
    | _ => throw "invalid parameter declaration"

/-- A function's return variables, an unnamed one named as `contract!` names
it: `_ret`, or `_ret0`, `_ret1`, … of several (Lean's spelling; KeY names
them `ret0`, `ret1`, …). -/
def retNames (f : SolcFun) : List (String × String) :=
  f.rets.zipIdx.map fun ((x, t), i) =>
    (if !x.isEmpty then x else if f.rets.length == 1 then "_ret" else s!"_ret{i}", t)

/-- Whether a loop in the statement, at any depth, has a `return` inside. -/
partial def hasLoopReturn (s : RawStmt) : Bool :=
  ((s matches .whileLoop .. | .forLoop .. | .doWhile .. | .loop ..) && s.hasReturn) ||
    s.blocks.any (·.any hasLoopReturn)

/-- A body's loops lowered (`lowerLoops`), solkey's `LoopLowering` after its
`ReturnLowering`: a `return` inside a loop becomes a flag, and the
`if (ret) return;` after the outermost loop is left to `lowerReturns`.  That
splices the loop's block, and a `for`'s declaration in it, over the
statements after it, so a body with such a loop is first renamed fresh past
its `nRets` return variables (`renameStmts`, as a call inlines it): a
sibling `for (uint i …)` then declares a name of its own. -/
def lowerBodyLoops (rets : List String) (nRets : Nat) (raw : List RawStmt) :
    ElabM (List RawStmt) := do
  let raw ← if raw.any hasLoopReturn then
      pure (raw.take nRets ++ (← renameStmts [] (raw.drop nRets)))
    else pure raw
  lowerLoops (some rets) raw

syntax (name := solcImport) "solc_import " str " hash " num " as " ident
  (" renaming " sepBy1(ident " => " ident, ", "))? (&" testing")?
  (&"evalOrder" term)? (&"entrypoints")? : command

/-- A large imported function table, compiled in bounded list segments.
For example, the testing import retains all of TestSuite's public functions.
Lean's list notation uses nested lets, so expose only the spine, retaining
the original heads. Every generated segment is checked by the kernel. -/
private def compileListSegments (owner : Lean.Name) (value : Expr) : TermElabM Expr := do
  let mut rest : Expr := ← whnf value
  let mut cells : Array Expr := #[]
  while rest.isAppOfArity ``List.cons 3 do
    cells := cells.push rest
    rest ← whnf rest.appArg!
  -- Small fields can be projections from a record update of the entire
  -- contract. Rebuild their exposed spine too (or return the weak-head value
  -- for a non-list), so native code need not compile that discarded record.
  let mut rebuilt : Expr := rest
  let mut count : Nat := 0
  for cell in cells.reverse do
    rebuilt := cell.appFn!.app rebuilt
    count := count + 1
    if cells.size > 64 && count % 64 == 0 then
      let name ← mkFreshUserName (owner ++ `_list)
      addAndCompile <| .defnDecl {
        name, levelParams := [], type := ← inferType rebuilt, value := rebuilt,
        hints := .abbrev, safety := .safe }
      rebuilt := mkConst name
  return rebuilt

/-- Attach compiler identities after the syntax macro has built the function table. -/
private def attachSourceDeclarations (model : Contract)
    (declarations : List (String × SourceFunction)) : Contract :=
  { model with funs := model.funs.map fun entry =>
      (entry.1, { entry.2 with sourceDecl := Semantics.lookupBy entry.1 declarations }) }

/-- Define an imported contract such as `TestSuite` without compiling its
whole function table in one expression. A kernel-checked reflexivity proof
certifies that segmentation preserves the complete original contract. -/
private def defineImportedContract (name : Lean.Name) (contractSyntax : Syntax) : TermElabM Unit := do
  let original ← elabTermEnsuringType contractSyntax (mkConst ``Contract)
  synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing
  let original ← instantiateMVars original
  let original ← whnf original
  unless original.isAppOf ``Contract.mk do
    throwError "solc_import: expected a contract literal"
  let mut fields : Array Expr := #[]
  for arg in original.getAppArgs do
    fields := fields.push (← compileListSegments name arg)
  let value : Expr := mkAppN original.getAppFn fields
  let certificate ← mkFreshUserName (name ++ `_inputEq)
  -- Check in the kernel directly: a metaprogram's recursive comparison of
  -- the full unsegmented table would itself exceed the elaborator's depth.
  addDecl <| .thmDecl {
    name := certificate, levelParams := [],
    type := mkApp3 (mkConst ``Eq [1]) (mkConst ``Contract) original value,
    value := mkApp2 (mkConst ``Eq.refl [1]) (mkConst ``Contract) original }
  addAndCompile <| .defnDecl {
    name, levelParams := [], type := mkConst ``Contract, value,
    hints := .regular 0, safety := .safe }

/-! Renaming specification parameters is a syntax operation. In particular,
quantified variables shadow parameters, and member labels are not variables. -/

private partial def specCommentTokens (depth : Nat) : List String → List String × List String
  | [] => ([], [])
  | "/" :: "-" :: rest =>
    let (body, tail) := specCommentTokens (depth + 1) rest
    (["/", "-"] ++ body, tail)
  | "-" :: "/" :: rest =>
    if depth == 1 then (["-", "/"], rest) else
      let (body, tail) := specCommentTokens (depth - 1) rest
      (["-", "/"] ++ body, tail)
  | token :: rest =>
    let (body, tail) := specCommentTokens depth rest
    (token :: body, tail)

/-- Preserve literal contents while escaping source identifiers around them. -/
private partial def specStringTokens : List String → List String × List String
  | [] => ([], [])
  | "\\" :: token :: rest =>
    let (body, tail) := specStringTokens rest
    (["\\", token] ++ body, tail)
  | "\"" :: rest => (["\""], rest)
  | token :: rest =>
    let (body, tail) := specStringTokens rest
    (token :: body, tail)

private partial def escapeSpecBindings (names : List String) : List String → List String
  | [] => []
  | "\"" :: rest =>
    let (body, tail) := specStringTokens rest
    "\"" :: body ++ escapeSpecBindings names tail
  | "\\" :: keyword :: rest => "\\" :: keyword :: escapeSpecBindings names rest
  | "«" :: rest =>
    let quoted := rest.takeWhile (· != "»")
    let tail := rest.drop quoted.length
    match tail with
    | [] => "«" :: quoted
    | closing :: tail => "«" :: quoted ++ closing :: escapeSpecBindings names tail
  | "-" :: "-" :: rest =>
    let comment := rest.takeWhile (· != "\n")
    ["-", "-"] ++ comment ++ escapeSpecBindings names (rest.drop comment.length)
  | "/" :: "-" :: rest =>
    let (comment, tail) := specCommentTokens 1 rest
    ["/", "-"] ++ comment ++ escapeSpecBindings names tail
  | token :: rest =>
    let token := ".".intercalate (token.splitOn "." |>.map fun name =>
      if name.contains '$' || (names.contains name && leanKeywords.contains name)
      then s!"«{name}»" else name)
    token :: escapeSpecBindings names rest

private partial def renameSpecSyntax (params rets : List (String × String)) (stx : Syntax) : Syntax :=
  match stx with
  | `(spec_expr| $key \in $_T:ident ($x:ident; $items:spec_expr,*; $guard)) =>
    -- The key and domain remain outside the guard's binder scope.
    let bound := x.getId.toString false
    let key' := renameSpecSyntax params rets key
    let guard' := renameSpecSyntax (params.filter (·.1 != bound)) (rets.filter (·.1 != bound)) guard
    let items' := items.elemsAndSeps.map (renameSpecSyntax params rets)
    stx.setArg 0 key' |>.setArg 7 (stx[7].setArgs items') |>.setArg 9 guard'
  | `(spec_expr| \forall $T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    let _ := T
    stx.setArg (stx.getNumArgs - 1)
      (renameSpecSyntax (params.filter (·.1 != (x.getId.toString false)))
        (rets.filter (·.1 != (x.getId.toString false))) body.raw)
  | `(spec_expr| \exists $T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    let _ := T
    stx.setArg (stx.getNumArgs - 1)
      (renameSpecSyntax (params.filter (·.1 != (x.getId.toString false)))
        (rets.filter (·.1 != (x.getId.toString false))) body.raw)
  | `(spec_expr| \old($body)) =>
    stx.setArg (stx.getNumArgs - 2) (renameSpecSyntax params [] body.raw)
  | `(spec_expr| $x:ident) =>
    match x.getId.components.map (·.toString false) with
    | head :: tail =>
      match Semantics.lookupBy head (params ++ rets) with
      | none => stx
      | some renamed =>
        let name := (renamed :: tail).foldl Lean.Name.str .anonymous
        let ident := Syntax.ident x.raw.getHeadInfo (name.toString.toSubstring) name []
        match stx with
        | .node info kind args => .node info kind (args.map fun a => if a == x.raw then ident else a)
        | _ => ident
    | [] => stx
  | _ =>
    match stx with
    | .node info kind args => .node info kind (args.map (renameSpecSyntax params rets))
    | _ => stx

private def rewriteSpecBindings (env : Environment) (sourceNames : List String) (kind : String)
    (params rets : List (String × String)) (text : String) : Except String String := do
  let names := params ++ rets
  if !["requires", "ensures", "invariant", "assignable"].contains kind then
    return text
  let escaped := String.join (escapeSpecBindings (sourceNames ++ names.map Prod.fst) (specTokens text))
  let stx ← Parser.runParserCategory env `sol_member s!"{kind} {escaped};"
  let some member := (renameSpecSyntax params (if kind == "ensures" then rets else []) stx).reprint
    | throw "renamed specification cannot be printed"
  -- Keep the reader's raw directive/text representation; validation parses
  -- the complete member again before it can enter a contract.
  let member := member.trim
  let directivePrefix := kind ++ " "
  unless member.startsWith directivePrefix && member.endsWith ";" do
    throw "renamed specification has an unexpected member shape"
  return (member.drop directivePrefix.length).take (member.length - directivePrefix.length - 1)

private partial def renameLoopSyntax (names : List (String × String)) (stx : Syntax) : Syntax :=
  match stx with
  | `(sol_loop_clause| /// @custom:key invariant \forall $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    stx.setArg (stx.getNumArgs - 1)
      (renameLoopSyntax (names.filter (·.1 != (x.getId.toString false))) body)
  | `(sol_loop_inv| \forall $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    stx.setArg (stx.getNumArgs - 1)
      (renameLoopSyntax (names.filter (·.1 != (x.getId.toString false))) body)
  | `(sol_expr| $x:ident) =>
    match x.getId.components.map (·.toString false) with
    | head :: tail =>
      match Semantics.lookupBy head names with
      | none => stx
      | some renamed =>
        let name := (renamed :: tail).foldl Lean.Name.str .anonymous
        let ident := Syntax.ident x.raw.getHeadInfo (name.toString.toSubstring) name []
        match stx with
        | .node info kind args => .node info kind (args.map fun a => if a == x.raw then ident else a)
        | _ => ident
    | [] => stx
  | _ =>
    match stx with
    | .node info kind args => .node info kind (args.map (renameLoopSyntax names))
    | _ => stx

private def rewriteLoopBindings (env : Environment) (sourceNames : List String) (names : List (String × String))
    (text : String) : Except String String := do
  let text := text.trim
  let directive := text.takeWhile (!Char.isWhitespace ·)
  unless ["invariant", "decreases"].contains directive do return text
  let escaped := String.join (escapeSpecBindings (sourceNames ++ names.map Prod.fst) (specTokens text))
  let stx ← Parser.runParserCategory env `sol_loop_clause ("/// @custom:key " ++ escaped)
  let some clause := (renameLoopSyntax names stx).reprint
    | throw "renamed loop specification cannot be printed"
  let clausePrefix := "/// @custom:key "
  unless clause.startsWith clausePrefix do throw "renamed loop clause has an unexpected shape"
  return clause.drop clausePrefix.length

private def specEnvironment (root member : String) : List Language.Feature :=
  match root, member with
  | "block", "timestamp" => [.blockTimestamp]
  | "block", "number" => [.blockNumber]
  | "block", "coinbase" => [.blockCoinbase]
  | "block", "difficulty" => [.blockDifficulty]
  | "block", "prevrandao" => [.blockPrevrandao]
  | "block", "gaslimit" => [.blockGaslimit]
  | "block", "chainid" => [.blockChainid]
  | "block", "basefee" => [.blockBasefee]
  | "block", "blobbasefee" => [.blockBlobbasefee]
  | "block", "slotnum" => [.blockSlotnum]
  | "msg", "data" | "msg", "sig" => [.rawCalldata]
  | "msg", "sender" => [.msgSender]
  | "msg", "value" => [.msgValue]
  | "tx", "origin" => [.txOrigin]
  | "tx", "gasprice" => [.txGasprice]
  | _, _ => []

private partial def specRoot (stx : Syntax) : Option String :=
  match stx with
  | `(spec_expr| $x:ident) => some (x.getId.toString false)
  | `(spec_expr| ($a)) => specRoot a
  | `(sol_expr| $x:ident) => some (x.getId.toString false)
  | `(sol_expr| ($a)) => specRoot a
  | _ => none

/-- Inspect parsed specification identifiers, respecting quantifier binders.
String literals and comments contain no identifier syntax to inspect. -/
private partial def specFeatures (bound : List String) (stx : Syntax) : List Source.Use :=
  let uses (root member : String) :=
    if bound.contains root then [] else (specEnvironment root member).map (⟨·, 0⟩)
  match stx with
  | `(spec_expr| $key \in $_T:ident ($x:ident; $items:spec_expr,*; $guard)) =>
    specFeatures bound key ++ items.elemsAndSeps.toList.flatMap (specFeatures bound) ++
      specFeatures ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) guard
  | `(spec_expr| \forall $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    specFeatures ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) body
  | `(spec_expr| \exists $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    specFeatures ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) body
  | `(sol_loop_clause| /// @custom:key invariant \forall $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    specFeatures ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) body
  | `(sol_loop_inv| \forall $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    specFeatures ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) body
  | `(spec_expr| $a:spec_expr.$f:ident) =>
    ((specRoot a).toList.flatMap fun root => uses root (f.getId.toString false)) ++
      specFeatures bound a
  | `(spec_expr| $x:ident) =>
    match x.getId.components.map (·.toString false) with
    | root :: member :: _ => uses root member
    | _ => []
  | `(sol_expr| $a:sol_expr.$f:ident) =>
    ((specRoot a).toList.flatMap fun root => uses root (f.getId.toString false)) ++
      specFeatures bound a
  | `(sol_expr| $x:ident) =>
    match x.getId.components.map (·.toString false) with
    | root :: member :: _ => uses root member
    | _ => []
  | _ => stx.getArgs.toList.flatMap (specFeatures bound)

/-- Free root-name reads in parsed specifications. Binder scope applies to
the guard only; member labels are not root reads. -/
partial def specReadsFreeName (name : String) (bound : List String) (stx : Syntax) : Bool :=
  let reads (x : Ident) :=
    let root := (x.getId.components.map (·.toString false)).headD ""
    root == name && !bound.contains root
  match stx with
  | `(spec_expr| $key \in $_T:ident ($x:ident; $items:spec_expr,*; $guard)) =>
    specReadsFreeName name bound key ||
      items.elemsAndSeps.any (specReadsFreeName name bound) ||
      specReadsFreeName name ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) guard
  | `(spec_expr| \forall $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    specReadsFreeName name ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) body
  | `(spec_expr| \exists $_T:ident $x:ident; $body) =>
    specReadsFreeName name ((x.getId.toString false) :: bound) body
  | `(spec_expr| $a:spec_expr.$_f:ident) => specReadsFreeName name bound a
  | `(spec_expr| $x:ident) => reads x
  | `(spec_loc| $a:spec_loc.$_f:ident) => specReadsFreeName name bound a
  | `(spec_loc| $x:ident) => reads x
  | _ => stx.getArgs.any (specReadsFreeName name bound)

private def readsSpecification (env : Environment) (sourceNames : List String)
    (name kind : String) (bound : List String) (text : String) : Except String Bool := do
  unless ["requires", "ensures", "invariant", "assignable"].contains kind do return false
  let escaped := String.join (escapeSpecBindings sourceNames (specTokens text))
  let parsed ← Parser.runParserCategory env `sol_member s!"{kind} {escaped};"
  pure (specReadsFreeName name bound parsed)

private def scanSpecifications (env : Environment) (sourceNames : List String)
    (request : Source.AdmissionRequest) : Source.ScopeScan :=
  request.specifications.foldl (fun scan (bound, text) =>
    let escaped := String.join (escapeSpecBindings sourceNames (specTokens text))
    let category := if escaped.startsWith "///" then `sol_loop_clause else `sol_member
    match Parser.runParserCategory env category escaped with
    | .ok parsed =>
      let uses := specFeatures bound parsed
      let classified := Source.ScopeScan.certify uses
      let envRoots := uses.map fun use =>
        let id := use.feature.id
        if id.startsWith "msg" || use.feature == .rawCalldata then "msg"
        else if id.startsWith "block" then "block"
        else if id.startsWith "tx" then "tx" else ""
      let collision := envRoots.any fun root => !root.isEmpty && request.modelBindings.contains root
      let classified := if collision then classified.append (.rejected [] {
        kind := .missingImplementation
        name := `solidity.lexicalSpecification
        reason := "an inherited builtin observation is shadowed in the executing contract"
        line := J.line request.entry }) else classified
      scan.append classified
    | .error message => scan.append (.rejected [] {
        kind := .missingImplementation, name := `solidity.specification,
        reason := message, line := J.line request.entry })) default

/-- The text of a contract with these members. -/
private def contractText (members : List String) : String :=
  s!"contract!\{ {" ".intercalate members} }"

/-- Why `s` does not elaborate as a contract, if it does not. -/
private def contractError? (s : Syntax) : TermElabM (Option String) :=
  withEnableInfoTree false <| withoutErrToSorry do
    tryCatchRuntimeEx (withCurrHeartbeats do
        let _ ← elabTermEnsuringType s (Lean.mkConst ``Contract)
        synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing
        pure none)
      fun ex => do pure (some (← ex.toMessageData.toString))

/-- Why a function calling `calls` is left out, if one of them is. -/
private def callsLeftOut? (bad : List (String × String)) (calls : List String) : Option String :=
  calls.findSome? fun g =>
    (Semantics.lookupBy g bad).map fun m => s!"it calls `{g}`, which is left out: {m}"

/-- Keep source admission setup separate from command generation. -/
private def readImportedContract (ast : Json) (name : String)
    (ren : List (String × String)) (testing entrypoints : Bool)
    (env : Environment) (sourceNames : List String) (provenance : Source.Provenance)
    (compilerCode : List (Int × (String × String))) (namedErrorSourceOrder : Bool) :
    Except String SolcContract :=
  readContract ast name ren testing
    (rewriteSpecBindings env sourceNames) (rewriteLoopBindings env sourceNames)
    (if provenance.legacyFixture then fun _ => default else fun request =>
      (Admission.scan ast provenance { request with
        declarationRoots := request.declarationRoots ++
          [Admission.header [] ast] ++ (J.arrD ast "nodes").toList.filter (J.kind · == "PragmaDirective") }).append
        (scanSpecifications env sourceNames request) |>.normalize |>.requireCompilerCode (!compilerCode.isEmpty))
    (fun bound modelBindings text => if provenance.legacyFixture then default else
      scanSpecifications env sourceNames {
        entry := .null, evaluatedRoots := [], modelBindings,
        specifications := [(bound, "/// @custom:key " ++ text)] })
    (readsSpecification env sourceNames) entrypoints
    (!provenance.legacyFixture && provenance.pipeline == some .viaIR) compilerCode namedErrorSourceOrder

private structure ImportedMembers where
  members : List String
  bad : List (String × String)
  ctorRow : Option ImportRow
  ctorMember : Option String

/-- Validate shared helper declarations and deployment before generating rows. -/
private def prepareImportedMembers (c : SolcContract) (srcName : String)
    (parse : Lean.Name → String → Except String Syntax) : CommandElabM ImportedMembers := do
  -- the functions called, each checked alone first: one that does not
  -- expand is left out, with every function that calls it
  -- A malformed unused modifier must not enter every function's wrapper.
  -- Its users still fail expansion because the named modifier is absent.
  let modifierMembers := c.modifierMembers.filter fun m =>
    match parse `sol_member m with | .ok _ => true | .error _ => false
  -- A helper header may return or accept a source struct/enum. Validate it
  -- in the same type-declaration context as the final contract; no state
  -- initializer or other helper body is admitted by this precheck.
  let typeMembers := c.members.filter fun member =>
    member.startsWith "struct " || member.startsWith "enum "
  let mut funMembers : Array String := #[]
  let mut badMembers : List (String × String) := []
  for (g, m) in c.funMembers do
    let calls := ((c.funs.find? (·.name == g)).map (·.calls)).getD []
    let r ← match callsLeftOut? badMembers calls,
        parse `term (contractText (typeMembers ++ [" ".intercalate modifierMembers, m])) with
      | some e, _ => pure (some e)
      | none, .error e => pure (some s!"its declaration does not parse: {e}")
      | none, .ok s => liftTermElabM (contractError? s)
    match r with
    | none => funMembers := funMembers.push m
    | some e => badMembers := badMembers ++ [(g, e)]
  let at_ (f : SolcFun) (line : Nat) (msg : String) : String :=
    s!"{srcName}:{if line == 0 then f.line else line}: {msg}"
  -- the constructor, its member last (it may call every function): its row
  -- now if it is left out, else once its program is made
  let mut ctorRow : Option ImportRow := none
  let mut ctorMember : Option String := none
  if let some f := c.ctor then
    if let some m := callsLeftOut? badMembers f.calls then
      ctorRow := some (.ofFun f .unsupported (at_ f 0 m))
    else match f.body with
      | .error (.excluded m l) => ctorRow := some (.ofFun f .excluded (at_ f l m))
      | .error (.unsupported m l) => ctorRow := some (.ofFun f .unsupported (at_ f l m))
      | .ok ss => ctorMember := some (f.ctorMember (ss.map (·.2)))
  -- an implicit constructor's initializer that does not print, or calls a
  -- function left out: the initializers are left out, which a deployment of
  -- `N` would not run
  if c.ctor.isNone then
    if let some g := c.initGap then
      logWarning m!"solc_import: the initializers are left out: {g.msg}"
  -- the contract, with the initializers and the constructor if it expands
  -- with them, else without
  let plain := c.members ++ modifierMembers ++ funMembers.toList
  let mut memberList := plain
  -- a declared constructor left out takes the initializers with it: the
  -- implicit one would run them alone
  if (ctorMember.isSome || c.initMembers != c.members) && (c.ctor.isNone || ctorMember.isSome) then
    let full := c.initMembers ++ modifierMembers ++ funMembers.toList ++ ctorMember.toList
    let r ← match parse `term (contractText full) with
      | .error e => pure (some s!"it does not parse: {e}")
      | .ok s => liftTermElabM (contractError? s)
    match r, c.ctor, ctorMember with
    | none, _, _ => memberList := full
    | some e, some f, some _ =>
      ctorRow := some (.ofFun f .unsupported
        (at_ f 0 s!"the contract with its constructor and initializers: {e}"))
      ctorMember := none
    | some e, _, _ =>
      -- An implicit initializer that renders but fails native elaboration
      -- must remain a deployment refusal, not a warning and default state.
      let f : SolcFun := {
        name := "constructor", sourceName := "constructor", sourceSignature := "constructor()",
        line := 0, tag := .diamond, params := [], body := .ok [] }
      ctorRow := some (.ofFun f .unsupported
        (at_ f 0 s!"the contract with its initializers: {e}"))
  pure { members := memberList, bad := badMembers, ctorRow, ctorMember }

@[command_elab solcImport]
def elabSolcImport : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let ref := stx
  let path : String := stx[1].isStrLit?.getD ""
  let expected : Nat := stx[3].isNatLit?.getD 0
  let N : Lean.Name := stx[5].getId
  let ren : List (String × String) :=
    if stx[6].getNumArgs > 0 then
      stx[6][1].getSepArgs.toList.map fun p => ((p[0].getId.toString false), (p[2].getId.toString false))
    else []
  let file := System.FilePath.mk (← getFileName)
  let fixture := (file.parent.getD ".") / path
  let bytes ← IO.FS.readBinFile fixture
  let h := fnv1a64 bytes
  unless h.toNat == expected do
    throwError "{path} has the hash {hex16 h}, not the one named: \
      re-run scripts/solc-ast.mjs, which rewrites the literal"
  let some text := String.fromUTF8? bytes | throwError "{path} is not UTF-8"
  let j ← ofExcept (Json.parse text)
  let ast ← ofExcept (j.getObjVal? "ast")
  let provenance ← ofExcept (Source.read j ast)
  let compilerCode ← ofExcept (Source.readCompilerCode j ast provenance)
  let source := ((j.getObjVal? "header").toOption.bind fun hd =>
    (hd.getObjValAs? String "source").toOption).getD "?"
  let srcName := (System.FilePath.mk source).fileName.getD source
  let env ← getEnv
  -- Quotation names are not semantic specification bindings.
  let sourceNames := (J.nodes ast).filterMap (J.str? · "name")
    |>.flatMap (·.splitOn ".") |>.eraseDups
  let legacyOrderOverride : Option EvalOrder ←
    if provenance.legacyFixture && !stx[8].isNone then
      liftTermElabM do
        let t ← Term.elabTermEnsuringType stx[8][1] (mkConst ``EvalOrder)
        let v ← unsafe evalExpr EvalOrder (mkConst ``EvalOrder) t
        pure (some v)
    else pure none
  let namedErrorSourceOrder := (legacyOrderOverride.map (·.binaryLeftToRight)).getD
    (provenance.pipeline == some .viaIR)
  let c ← ofExcept (readImportedContract ast N.getString! ren (!stx[7].isNone)
    (!stx[9].isNone) env sourceNames provenance compilerCode namedErrorSourceOrder)
  let parse (cat : Lean.Name) (s : String) : Except String Syntax :=
    (Parser.runParserCategory env cat s).map (atRef ref)
  if !stx[7].isNone then
    -- A clause must parse alone. Otherwise `ensures false; requires false`
    -- could inject a second member and turn a failing specification vacuous.
    for m in c.members do
      let _ ← ofExcept (parse `sol_member m)
    for f in c.funs ++ c.ctor.toList do
      -- A refused body contributes no member or specification. Keep its
      -- unsupported row local, even when its unimported clause needs a
      -- renamed parameter (such as Solidity's `from`).
      if let .ok _ := f.body then
        for (kind, text) in f.specClauses do
          let _ ← ofExcept (parse `sol_member s!"{kind} {text};")
  let prepared ← prepareImportedMembers c srcName parse
  let memberList := prepared.members
  let badMembers := prepared.bad
  let mut ctorRow := prepared.ctorRow
  let ctorMember := prepared.ctorMember
  let at_ (f : SolcFun) (line : Nat) (msg : String) : String :=
    s!"{srcName}:{if line == 0 then f.line else line}: {msg}"
  let ctStx ← ofExcept (parse `term (contractText memberList))
  let ctStx ← if c.internalFuns.isEmpty then pure ctStx else
    let markers : List (String × Nat) := c.internalFuns.map fun name => (name ++ "#internalEntry", 0)
    liftTermElabM <| `(let model : Contract := $(⟨ctStx⟩)
      { model with widths := $(quote markers) ++ model.widths })
  let ctStx ← if c.sourceDecls.isEmpty then pure ctStx else do
    let metadataName ← liftTermElabM do
      let name ← mkFreshUserName (N ++ `_sourceDecls)
      let value : Expr := toExpr c.sourceDecls
      let valueTy : Expr ← inferType value
      addAndCompile <| .defnDecl {
        name
        levelParams := []
        type := valueTy
        value
        hints := .regular 0
        safety := .safe }
      pure name
    liftTermElabM <| `(attachSourceDeclarations $(⟨ctStx⟩) $(mkIdent metadataName))
  let ctStx ← if provenance.legacyFixture then
      match legacyOrderOverride with
      | none => pure ctStx
      | some order => do
        let eo ← liftTermElabM <| `(Solidity.EvalOrder.mk
          $(quote order.binaryLeftToRight) $(quote order.modularLeftToRight) $(quote order.modifierFrames))
        liftTermElabM <| `(({ $(⟨ctStx⟩) with evalOrder := $eo } : Contract))
    else do
      unless stx[8].isNone do
        throwError "modern source imports take evaluation order from their compiler provenance"
      if provenance.pipeline == some .viaIR then
        liftTermElabM <| `(({ $(⟨ctStx⟩) with evalOrder := EvalOrder.viaIR } : Contract))
      else
        liftTermElabM <| `(({ $(⟨ctStx⟩) with evalOrder := Solidity.EvalOrder.mk false false false } : Contract))
  liftTermElabM <| defineImportedContract N ctStx
  -- each body, read by the macros to a `List RawStmt` term
  let rawTy := mkApp (mkConst ``List [0]) (mkConst ``RawStmt)
  let mut rows : Array ImportRow := #[]
  let mut raws : Array (Nat × SolcFun × List (Nat × String) × Expr) := #[]
  for f in c.funs do
    let row := ImportRow.ofFun f
    if f.tag == .skip then
      rows := rows.push (row .skipped (at_ f 0 "tagged `@custom:key skip`"))
      continue
    if let some m := callsLeftOut? badMembers f.calls then
      rows := rows.push (row .unsupported (at_ f 0 m))
      continue
    match f.body with
    | .error (.excluded m l) => rows := rows.push (row .excluded (at_ f l m))
    | .error (.unsupported m l) => rows := rows.push (row .unsupported (at_ f l m))
    | .ok ss =>
      let ss := if f.modifierApps.isEmpty then ss else
        [(f.line, s!"{identText f.name}({", ".intercalate (f.params.map (identText ∘ Prod.fst))})")]
      -- its return variables first, at their defaults
      let ss := (retNames f).map (fun (x, t) => (f.line, s!"{t} {identText x}")) ++ ss
      -- a `calldata` parameter a memory local (`calldataCheck`, below)
      let params := f.params.map fun (x, t) =>
        s!"{if t.endsWith " calldata" then t.dropRight 9 ++ " memory" else t} {identText x}; "
      let text := "sol_raw!{ " ++ String.join params ++ String.join (ss.map fun (_, s) => s ++ "; ") ++ "}"
      match parse `term text with
      | .error e => rows := rows.push (row .unsupported (at_ f 0 s!"the printed text does not parse: {e}"))
      | .ok s =>
        -- no info trees: the server would keep every expansion, all at this command
        let r ← liftTermElabM <| withEnableInfoTree false <| withoutErrToSorry do
          tryCatchRuntimeEx (withCurrHeartbeats do
              let e ← elabTermEnsuringType s rawTy
              synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing
              let e ← instantiateMVars e
              if e.hasMVar then pure (Except.error "the macros leave a hole")
              else pure (.ok e))
            fun ex => do pure (.error (← ex.toMessageData.toString))
        match r with
        | .error m => rows := rows.push (row .unsupported (at_ f 0 m))
        | .ok e =>
          raws := raws.push (rows.size, f, ss, e)
          rows := rows.push (row .elaborated "")
  -- the contract and every body, evaluated once
  let pairTy := mkApp2 (mkConst ``Prod [0, 0]) (mkConst ``Contract)
    (mkApp (mkConst ``List [0]) rawTy)
  let val := mkApp4 (mkConst ``Prod.mk [0, 0]) (mkConst ``Contract)
    (mkApp (mkConst ``List [0]) rawTy) (mkConst N) (← liftTermElabM <| mkListLit rawTy (raws.map (·.2.2.2)).toList)
  let (C, bodies) ← liftTermElabM <| unsafe evalExpr (Contract × List (List RawStmt)) pairTy val
  -- the typed elaborator on each, the program quoted back and checked
  for ((k, f, ss, _), raw) in raws.toList.zip bodies do
    let fail (msg : String) : Array ImportRow :=
      rows.set! k { rows[k]! with status := .unsupported, reason := msg }
    -- its loops, then its `return`s lowered, which moves statements: an
    -- error is then the function's
    let (params, raw) := raw.splitAt f.params.length
    let lower := !f.rets.isEmpty || raw.any RawStmt.hasReturn
    let rets := (retNames f).map (·.1)
    let lowered : ECtx → Except String (List RawStmt × (ECtx × Nat)) := fun Γ => do
      let (raw, st) ← (lowerBodyLoops rets rets.length raw).runFrom { funs := C.funs }
        (Γ, RawStmt.maxIdxs raw + 1)
      pure ((← if lower then lowerReturns rets raw else pure raw), st)
    -- its `calldata` parameters read only (`calldataCheck`)
    let cd := f.params.filterMap fun (x, t) => if t.endsWith " calldata" then some x else none
    let refRets := (retNames f).filterMap fun (x, t) =>
      if t.endsWith " memory" || t.endsWith " storage" then some x else none
    let scope := (calldataCheck C.funs 8 cd refRets raw).bind fun _ => paramCtx C params
    if let .ok Γ := scope then rows := rows.set! k { rows[k]! with paramTypes := (ECtx.toNCtx Γ).ctx }
    match scope >>= lowered with
    | .error m => rows := fail (at_ f 0 m)
    | .ok (raw, st) =>
      match elabProgAtS.go C 0 raw st (source := true) with
      | .error (j, m) =>
        rows := fail (at_ f (if lower then 0 else (ss[j]?.map (·.1)).getD 0) m)
      | .ok ⟨_, P⟩ =>
        let n : Lean.Name := N ++ Lean.Name.mkSimple f.name
        match ← liftCoreM (Prog.define n N P) with
        | none => pure ()
        | some m => rows := fail (at_ f 0 m)
  -- the constructor's program, a deployment: `constructor(x̄);` with its
  -- parameters in scope (`elabCtor`), the obligation's program
  if let (some f, some _) := (c.ctor, ctorMember) then
    let row := ImportRow.ofFun f
    if f.tag == .skip then
      ctorRow := some (row .skipped (at_ f 0 "tagged `@custom:key skip`"))
    else
      let raw : List RawStmt := [.call (.name "constructor") (f.params.map fun (x, _) => RawExpr.name x)]
      match (C.ctor.getD { params := [], body := [] }).paramCtx with
      | .error m => ctorRow := some (row .unsupported (at_ f 0 m))
      | .ok Γ =>
        let row := fun st msg => { (row st msg) with paramTypes := (ECtx.toNCtx Γ).ctx }
        match elabProgAtS.go C 0 raw (Γ, RawStmt.maxIdxs raw + 1) (source := true) with
        | .error (_, m) => ctorRow := some (row .unsupported (at_ f 0 m))
        | .ok ⟨_, P⟩ =>
          let n : Lean.Name := N ++ Lean.Name.mkSimple f.name
          match ← liftCoreM (Prog.define n N P) with
          | none => ctorRow := some (row .elaborated "")
          | some m => ctorRow := some (row .unsupported (at_ f 0 m))
  -- not compiled: compiling the scoped literals costs about half the import
  -- (TestSuite: 5.9 s); a reader evaluates a program's value (`#solc_show`,
  -- `Frontend/Problems.lean`'s `obligation`)
  let rowsTy := mkApp (mkConst ``List [0]) (mkConst ``ImportRow)
  let rep : Lean.Name := N ++ `report
  let reportRows := (ctorRow.toList ++ rows.toList).map fun row =>
    -- Older lowering code calls representation limits "excluded". Modern
    -- policy exclusions already have a scan diagnostic; the remaining cases
    -- are implementation gaps, independent of catalog inventory status.
    let row := if !provenance.legacyFixture && row.status == .excluded && row.sourceDiagnostic.isNone then
      { row with status := .unsupported } else row
    let sourceDiagnostic := row.sourceDiagnostic.orElse fun _ =>
      if row.status == .unsupported then some {
        kind := .missingImplementation, name := `solidity.lowering,
        reason := row.reason } else none
    { row with admissionChecked := !provenance.legacyFixture, sourceDiagnostic }
  -- A modern report retains source metadata at every row. Compile its large
  -- literal in bounded segments too, certifying the complete original list
  -- before exporting the report that tooling evaluates.
  let originalReport := toExpr reportRows
  let reportValue ← liftTermElabM do
    let value ← compileListSegments rep originalReport
    let certificate ← mkFreshUserName (rep ++ `_inputEq)
    addDecl <| .thmDecl {
      name := certificate, levelParams := [],
      type := mkApp3 (mkConst ``Eq [1]) rowsTy originalReport value,
      value := mkApp2 (mkConst ``Eq.refl [1]) rowsTy originalReport }
    pure value
  liftCoreM <| addAndCompile <| .defnDecl {
    name := rep, levelParams := [], type := rowsTy, value := reportValue,
    hints := .abbrev, safety := .safe }
  liftCoreM <| addAndCompile <| .defnDecl {
    name := rep ++ `provenance, levelParams := [], type := mkConst ``Source.Provenance,
    value := toExpr provenance,
    hints := .abbrev, safety := .safe }

/-- The value of the imported program `n` (a literal: the import does not
compile it), its contexts' terms and its parameters' names, newest first. -/
def programValue (n : Lean.Name) (r : ImportRow) : CoreM (Expr × Expr × Expr × List Var) := do
  let ci ← getConstInfo n
  let ty := ci.type.consumeMData
  unless ty.isAppOfArity ``Prog 3 && ci.value?.isSome do throwError "{n} is not a scoped program"
  pure (ci.value!, ty.appFn!.appArg!, ty.appArg!, r.params.reverse.map fun (x, _) => Var.ofName x)

/-- `#solc_show N.f`: the imported program `N.f`, one statement per line
(`Prog.show`, its parameters named), its value evaluated. -/
syntax (name := solcShow) "#solc_show " ident : command

@[command_elab solcShow]
def elabSolcShow : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let n ← liftCoreM <| realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo stx[1]
  let N := n.getPrefix
  let rows ← liftTermElabM <| unsafe evalConst (List ImportRow) (N ++ `report)
  let some r := rows.find? (·.declName N == n) | throwError "{n} is no row of {N}"
  let (v, _, _, ns) ← liftCoreM <| programValue n r
  logInfo (← liftTermElabM do
    unsafe evalExpr String (mkConst ``String) (← mkAppM ``Prog.show #[toExpr ns, v]))
